body.translated_text: <s>Sāṃkhyatattvavivecana</s> (Investigation of the Sāṃkhya Categories), composed by <s>Śrī Ṣimānanda</s>.

children.translated_text: By the son of <s>Raghunandana</s>, a resident of <s>Iṣṭikāpura</s>,
by <s>Ṣimānanda</s>, foremost among the twice-born of <s>Kānyakubja</s>, this is expounded. (1)
Homage to you, O <s>Kapila</s>, the great-souled originator of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>,
the promulgator of the knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (categories). (2)
'For one afflicted by the threefold suffering (<s>duḥkhatraya</s>), how may I find peace here?

children.text: tathopadiśa janmādi yathā na syāt kṛpānidhe // 3 //
children.translated_text: Instruct me, O treasury of compassion, so that birth and the rest may cease.' (3)

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭo muniḥ prāha nirviṇṇāya kṛpānidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus questioned, the sage, a treasury of compassion, spoke to the dispassionate one;
twenty-five <s>sūtras</s> have been explained by the great souls. (4)

children.text: babandhuḥ kavayaḥ kāvye vyācikhyuḥ kavayaḥ pare /
children.translated_text: Poets have composed them in verse, and other poets have elaborated upon them;
the true meaning of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teaching — that very thing is here investigated

body.translated_text: by the dull-witted <s>Ṣimānanda</s>, who is merely a belly-filler and the like. (5)
The <s>prakṛtis</s> (primary causes) are eight. (<s>Tats</s> 1)

children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense), the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), and the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs),
and the <s>bhūtas</s> (gross elements) — by general count, these are indeed twenty-four.

body.text:
eteṣveva dharmadharmyabhedena guṇakarmasāmānyānāmantarbhāvaḥ |
prakṛtitvaṃ ca sākṣātparamparayākhilavikāropādānatvam |
vyutpattistu prakṛṣṭā pariṇāmarūpā ākṛtirasyā iti |
sā ca sāmyāvasthayopalakṣitasattvādidravyatrayarūpā |
sāmyāvasthā ca śāntaghoramūḍhādirūpāṇāmapi asamudāyavadrūpatvepi atiśayaiḥ samudāyavadbhiravirodhena vartamānatvaṃ sāmānyātmanā guṇabhāvo 'tiśayātmanā prādhānyaṃ viśeṣātmanā vaiṣamyamityato nyūnādhikabhāvenāsaṃhatāvasthā 'kāryāvastheti yāvat |
mahadādikaṃ tu kāryasattvādikaṃ na kadāpyakāryāvasthaṃ bhavatīti tadvyāvṛttiḥ |
vaiṣamyāvasthāyāmapi prakṛtitvasiddhaye upalakṣitamityuktaṃ sattvādiguṇavatī prakṛtiḥ sattvādyanatiriktatvāt tathā ca sūtraṃ sattvādīnāmataddharmatvaṃ tadrūpatvāditi sattvādīnāṃ prakṛtisvarūpatvaṃ na tu prakṛtidharmatvam |
guṇebhya eva sarvakāryopapattau tadanyaprakṛtikalpanāvaiyarthyāt |
sūtrabhāṣyābhyāmapi tathoktatvāt |
yattu prakṛterguṇā itivat vanasya vṛkṣā itivat vyaṣṭisamaṣṭyabhiprāyeṇeti sattvaṃ rajastama iti prakṛterabhavan guṇā iti ca na sattvādīnāṃ prakṛtikāryatvavacanaṃ guṇanityatāvākyavirodhena mahattattvakāraṇībhūtakāryasattvādiparam |
mahadādisṛṣṭirguṇavaimyāt |
tacca sajātīyasaṃvalanena guṇāntaravyāvṛttaprakāśādiphalopahitaḥ sattvādivyavahārayogyaḥ pariṇāma iti sattvādivyavahāro vaiṣamya evetyāha śrutiḥ yathā tama evedamagra āsīt tatpare syāt pareṇeritaṃ viṣamatvaṃ(1) pratyayādvai rajaso(2) rūpaṃ tadrajaḥ khalvīritaṃ viṣamatvaṃ pratyayādvai sattvasya(3) rūpamiti sattvāditrayaṃ ca sattvādisvarūpamiti sattvāditrayaṃ ca sukhaprakāśalāghavaprasādādiguṇakatayā saṃyogavibhāgādimattayānāśritatvopādānatvādinā dravyatve 'pi puruṣopakāratvāt puruṣabandhakatvācca guṇaśabdenocyate indriyādivat guṇānāṃ sukhaduḥkamohātmakapravādastu dharmadharmyabhedāt manasaḥ saṅkalpātmakatvavat tatra sattvaṃ sukhaprasādaprakāśādyanekadharmakamapi pradhānatastu sukhātmakamucyate |
evaṃ rajo 'pi duḥkhakāluṣyapravṛtyādyanekadharmakaṃ prādhānyatastu duḥkhātmakamucyate |
evaṃ tamo 'pi mohāvaraṇastambhanādyanekadharmakaṃ prādhānyatastu mohātmakamucyate |
sato bhāvaḥ sattvaṃ dharmaprādhānyenottamaṃ puruṣopakaraṇaṃ rāgayogādrajo madhyamam |
tamodharmāvaraṇayogādadhamaṃ sattvādīnyasaṃkhyavyaktayaḥ pratikṣaṇapariṇāmitvāt laghutvādidharmairanyonyaṃ sādharmyaṃ vaidharmyaṃ ca guṇānāmasaṃkhyātamiti sūtrāt |

children.text: ekadānekapuruṣādisṛṣṭiśravaṇācca ekaikavyaktitve vibhutvaṃ syāt tathā ca saṃyogavaicitryābhāvādanantavaicitryaṃ kāryāṇāṃ na syāt |
children.translated_text: And since the creation of one and of many <s>puruṣas</s> is heard of, if each manifestation were single, it would have to be all-pervading; and then, due to the absence of variety in conjunction, the infinite variety of effects would not be possible.
Also because of the absence of a delimiting substance.

children.text: tasmādasaṃkhyātānyeva sattvādīni tritvakathanaṃ tu vibhājakopādhitrayeṇaiva vaiśeṣikāṇāṃ navadravyavacanavat sattvādīni ca yathāyogyamaṇuvibhuparimāṇakāni itarathā rajasaścalasvabhāvatvavacananirodhaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>sattva</s> and other [<s>guṇas</s>] are indeed innumerable. The mention of their being three is only through the three delimiting conditions, just as the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> speak of nine substances. And <s>sattva</s> and the others are, as appropriate, of atomic, all-pervading, or medium size; otherwise the statement that <s>rajas</s> has an inherently active nature would be contradicted.
Since it is fitting that the cause of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) be all-pervading, if all causal substances were all-pervading, the delimitation of effects would be impossible.

body.translated_text: Among these very [categories], by the distinction of property and property-bearer, the qualities and actions of the general [categories] are subsumed. Being a <s>prakṛti</s> (primary cause) means being the material cause of all modifications, either directly or indirectly. The etymological derivation is: that whose form (<s>ākṛti</s>) is distinguished (<s>prakṛṣṭā</s>) transformation. And that [<s>Prakṛti</s>] is indicated by the state of equilibrium [of the <s>guṇas</s>].

children.translated_text: That [<s>Prakṛti</s>] is devoid of sound and touch, and is not conjoined with form and the rest;
it is endowed with the three <s>guṇas</s>, it is the womb of the world, beginningless, and the source and dissolution [of all].

body.text:
ityādyukterna paramāṇvādāvantarbhāvaḥ prakṛteriti /
athaivamapi prakṛteraṇuvibhusādhāraṇasattvādyanekavyaktirūpatve aparicchinnatvaikatvākriyatvasaiddhāntakṣatiriti cenna kāraṇadravyatvasvarūpaprakṛtitvenaivāparicchinnatvavacanādgandhatvena gandhānāṃ pṛthivīvyāpakatāvat ākāśādiprakṛtīnāṃ vibhutvenaiva prakṛtivibhutvasiddhāntopapatteśca |
tathā puruṣabhedena sargabhedena ca bhedābhāvasyaiva ekaśabdārthatvāt |
ajāmekāmitiśrutestathāvagamāt |
tathādhyavasāyo 'bhimānādikriyārāhityasyaivākriyaśabdārthatvādityanyathā śrutismṛtityuktasya prakṛtikṣobhasyānupapatteriti |
tatrāyaṃ prayogaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakamahadādikāryaṃ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakadravyakāryaṃ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatvāt vastrādikāryaśayyāvaditi prakṛtau pramāṇam |
bāhyavastuṣu sukhādikamuttamatvādikameva ghaṭarūpamitivaccandanasukhaṃ strīsukhamityādipratyayācceti dik |
body.translated_text: Thus it is said — there is no subsumption of <s>Prakṛti</s> into atoms and the like. Now, even if <s>Prakṛti</s> has the form of multiple manifestations of <s>sattva</s> and the rest, whether atomic or all-pervading, the doctrinal positions of unlimitedness, oneness, and non-action are not undermined, since the essential nature of being a causal substance is <s>Prakṛti</s>.

children.translated_text: The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and the group of five <s>tanmātras</s> —
these eight are the <s>prakṛtis</s> (primary causes); and seven [of them] also attain the state of being modifications.
Because they are produced from the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), they are also called 'unmanifest';

children.text: vyajyante ca yathā loke ghaṭādyā na tathā hi tat //
children.translated_text: but they are not manifest in the world in the way that pots and such are — for it is not so.
The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, the Cause,
the Undesignated, the Flower of Darkness, the Field, the Imperishable — these are its names.
These names beginning with 'having many natures' (<s>bahudhātmaka</s>) — the wise have declared them of it.
Since it is not manifest through the senses, it is called 'unmanifest' (<s>avyakta</s>);
having no beginning, middle, or end, and being without distinguishing marks, it is so [called].

body.translated_text: The <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) itself declares this:

children.translated_text: Without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable,
likewise eternal, devoid of taste and smell,
without beginning or middle, beyond the Great (<s>Mahat</s>), permanent —
the wise declare this to be <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). Thus [ends the scriptural citation].
Therefore it is without any mark, subtle, and of the nature of production;

children.text: ekaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ tatra kāryaṃ kasyāpi netare //
children.translated_text: it is one, common [to all], and the effect therein belongs to no one else.
<s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Mahat</s> (the Great), <s>Manas</s> (mind), <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Mati</s> (thought), <s>Khyāti</s> (discernment), <s>Apūrvaka</s> (the unprecedented),
<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>Bhūti</s> (being), <s>Dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>Santati</s> (continuity), <s>Smṛti</s> (memory) — thus also [are its names].
The name 'of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>' indicates <s>Buddhi</s> as the Great (<s>Mahat</s>).
'From the <s>guṇas</s> being agitated, the three <s>Vedas</s> came into being.'

body.text:
ekā mūrttistrayo devā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ / iti
  viṣṇurevādisargeṣu svayaṃbhūrbhavati prabhuḥ //
body.translated_text: 'One form, three gods — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.' Thus, '<s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, in the primordial creations, becomes the self-born lord.'

children.text: atra sattvādyaṃśatrayeṇa mahato devatātrayopādhitvāttadavivekena tisra iti |
children.translated_text: Here, through the three portions of <s>sattva</s> and the rest, <s>Mahat</s> serves as the limiting adjunct of the triad of deities; through non-discrimination from it, [they appear as] three.

children.text: sāttvikāṃśāt pradhānāt tu mahattattvamajāyata iti mahattvasya prādhānyena cādhyavasāyo vṛttirmahadahaṃkāramanastritayātmakasyāntaḥkaraṇavṛkṣasya mahattattvaṃ bījāvasthā taduktaṃ sāṃkhyasūtre idameva mahattattvamaṃśato rajastamaḥsaṃbhedena pariṇataṃ sat vyaṣṭijīvānāmupādhiradharmādiyuktaṃ kṣudramapi bhavati mahaduparāgādviparītamiti |
children.translated_text: From the <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) portion of <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Mahat-tattva</s> (the Great Principle) was born. The primacy of greatness is determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) — the function of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) whose tree-form consists of <s>Mahat</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>; <s>Mahat-tattva</s> is the seed-state. As stated in the <s>Sāṃkhya Sūtra</s>: 'This alone is the —'

children.text: mahatastriguṇasvarūpatvāddehasya dehinā kālarūpaviṣṇunā kṣobhyadaśāyāṃ guṇarūpopādhiprādhānyādaviveke brahmaviṣṇuśivatvaṃ tatra mahān suṣuptyabhimānī śivastadupādhistamaḥkāryarūpī tatra svapnābhimānī viṣṇustadupādhiḥ kāryasattvaṃ tatra jāgradabhimānī brahmā tadupādhiḥ kāryarajaḥ tatra samudāyasamunnayananyāyena samaṣṭervyaṣṭyananyatvānmaśakādirapi viṣṇureveti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Because <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) is of the nature of the three <s>guṇas</s>, when the body is agitated by the embodied one, <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of time, due to the predominance of the limiting adjuncts in the form of the <s>guṇas</s>, in non-discrimination there is the nature of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>. Therein, <s>mahat</s> is the one whose self-identification is with deep sleep.
Creation proceeds in the sequence beginning with <s>mahat</s> only, not in the sequence beginning with the elements.
And that [is stated] in the <s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s>:
The <s>bhūtādi</s> (primal element), transforming, created the sound-<s>tanmātra</s> (subtle element of sound);
from that arose <s>ākāśa</s> (space), hollow in nature, characterized by sound.

children.text: ākāśaṃ tu vikurvāṇaḥ sparśamātraṃ sasarja ha /
children.translated_text: <s>Ākāśa</s>, transforming, created the touch-<s>tanmātra</s>;
from that <s>vāyu</s> (wind) arises, and touch is considered its quality.

body.text:
ityādi
nanvevaṃ cedākāśādīnāṃ kevalaṃ vikṛtitvaṃ kathaṃ tatra ākāśādīnāṃ sparśāditanmātreṣu ahaṃkāropaṣṭambhamātreṇa kāraṇatvasya purāṇādiṣūktatvāt |
body.translated_text: And so forth. Now, if this is so, how can <s>ākāśa</s> and the rest be merely modifications? Because the causality of <s>ākāśa</s> and the rest with respect to the <s>tanmātras</s> of touch and so on is stated in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and other texts as being merely through the support of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.

children.translated_text: This is not a man but a post—<s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is that which determines;
from the all-pervading [<s>pradhāna</s>] presided over by <s>Puruṣa</s>, the state of being <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) arises.
The power of consciousness (<s>cit-śakti</s>) is of such a nature—its function, mixed with <s>sattva</s>,
is of the nature of <s>rajas</s>, because of the triplication (<s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s>) taught in the <s>Śruti</s>.
Knowledge, <s>dharma</s>, dispassion, and sovereignty—these arise from <s>sattva</s>;
lack of sovereignty, lack of dispassion, <s>adharma</s>, and ignorance
are to be known as arising from <s>tamas</s>—these are declared to be the divisions of <s>buddhi</s>.
Knowledge is the understanding of reality; <s>dharma</s> is the observance of what is enjoined by the <s>Śruti</s>;
dispassion is non-attachment to objects; sovereignty is <s>aṇimā</s> and other [supernatural powers];
by the reverse of each of those respectively, the <s>tāmasic</s> four [are known].
Through knowledge comes liberation; through <s>dharma</s>, upward destiny;
through dispassion, dissolution into the imperishable; through sovereignty, unobstructed movement.
Thus this eightfold power called <s>buddhi</s> has been explained;
it is a modification of <s>pradhāna</s> and also the source of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.
It has been determined by the sages as <s>mūla-prakṛti</s> (root nature) and so forth;
if there is a desire to know this—that <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is one—then consider:
That which makes the word 'I' is remembered as <s>abhimāna</s> (self-conceit);

children.text: spṛśe 'haṃ rasaye vāhaṃ svāmī cāhaṃ mayā hṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'I touch,' 'I taste,' 'I am the master,' 'I have taken'—

children.text: ityādi nāma yasyāsīttasya bhedā amī śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: such are its names; hear now its divisions:
<s>Vaikārika</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>bhūtādi</s>, with the inferential (<s>sānumānaka</s>)
and the non-inferential (<s>niranumāna</s>)—these five are proclaimed as its divisions.
<s>Vaikārika</s> is <s>sāttvic</s>; <s>bhūtādi</s> is remembered as <s>tāmasic</s>;
<s>Taijasa</s> is to be known as <s>rājasic</s>. From that [<s>bhūtādi</s>], the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements);
the group of eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) arises from the <s>sāttvic</s> [<s>ahaṃkāra</s>].
The presiding deities are said to arise from the <s>taijasa</s> [<s>ahaṃkāra</s>];
if asked how this is so—it is because of the principle of triplication (<s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s>).
The sound-<s>tanmātra</s>—in it only sound is perceived;
no distinction such as <s>udātta</s> (high pitch), <s>niṣāda</s>, and others is perceived in it.
The touch-<s>tanmātra</s>—in it only touch is perceived;
no specific qualities such as cold, softness, and others are found in it.
Similarly with the form-<s>tanmātra</s> and likewise the taste-<s>tanmātra</s>;
and the smell-<s>tanmātra</s>—in these, no specific differentiation is perceived.
The <s>tanmātras</s>, being unspecified, are also called subtle elements (<s>sūkṣma-bhūtas</s>);
they are objects of experience, tranquil, fierce, and dull by nature, and indeed atomic.

body.translated_text: Because of their productive nature, the <s>prakṛtis</s> (primary causes) are proclaimed to be eight in number.
The sixteen modifications. [<s>Sāṃkhyatattvavivecana</s> 2]

children.translated_text: The eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) and the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements)—
these sixteen are modifications only, not possessed of the nature of primary cause.

children.text: śrotraṃ tvak cakṣūṣī jihvā ghrāṇaṃ jñānendriyaṃ tvidam /
children.translated_text: Ear, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose—these are the <s>jñānendriyas</s> (organs of knowledge);
speech, hands, excretory organ, generative organ, and feet are considered the <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action).

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ karma prakurvanti jñānaṃ ceti yathaiṣitam /
children.translated_text: Each performs its own respective function, and [they produce] knowledge, as desired;
and <s>manas</s> (mind), which is of a dual nature, has the character of volition (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) and so forth.
The <s>indriyas</s> are instruments (<s>karaṇas</s>)—a stream composed of the <s>vaikārika</s> (<s>sāttvic ahaṃkāra</s>);
they are called 'fixed stations' (<s>padas</s>) and '<s>akṣas</s>' (imperishable faculties).
Earth, water, fire, wind, and space—
these five alone are the <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements), serving the purpose of supporting and so forth.
Water serves the other four through its cohesive nature;
fire through its cooking nature; wind through its carrying nature.
Earth, possessing the five qualities beginning with sound, is considered to have five qualities;
water possesses the qualities beginning with sound but is devoid of smell;
fire possesses sound, touch, and form; wind, however,

children.text: śabdaśca sparśa ityevamākāśe śabda eva tu //
children.translated_text: possesses sound and touch; and in <s>ākāśa</s> (space), there is sound alone.
But the gross elements are not such—they have specific forms;
the modifications are declared to be of three kinds: tranquil (<s>śānta</s>), fierce (<s>ghora</s>), and dull (<s>mūḍha</s>).

body.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s>. [<s>Sāṃkhyatattvavivecana</s> 3]

children.translated_text: Because of lying in the city (body), because of being the measure, because of filling, because of dwelling abundantly—
he is beginningless, all-pervading, conscious, without qualities, and supreme.
He is the seer, the experiencer, the knower of the field, pure, and not subject to production;
he is subtle, eternal, indeed without beginning, without middle, and without end.
Because everything is pervaded by him, therefore he is all-pervading;
and because he possesses the perception of pleasure, he is conscious; and likewise without qualities.
Because of being devoid of qualities such as <s>sattva</s>, he is remembered as supreme by virtue of his transcendence;
he is the seer because of his connection with the visible <s>prakṛti</s>, and the experiencer because of experiencing.

children.text: kṣetre guṇagataṃ vetti kṣetrajña iti kīrttitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He knows what pertains to the <s>guṇas</s> in the field, hence he is proclaimed as <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field);
because of the absence of contact with good, evil, and the like, he is considered pure.
Because of being seedless, he does not produce—thus he is not subject to production;
because of being without parts and beyond the senses, he is subtle; he is eternal because of being everlasting.

children.text: evaṃ sāṃkhyaḥ sa puruṣo vyākhyātaḥ pūrvasūribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Puruṣa</s> in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> has been explained by the ancient sages.

children.text: jīvo jantuḥ pumānātmā puruṣaḥ pūjako naraḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Jīva</s>, <s>jantu</s> (living being), <s>pumān</s> (man), <s>ātman</s> (self), <s>puruṣa</s>, worshipper, <s>nara</s> (person),

children.text: kṣetrajñaścākṣaraḥ prāṇaḥ koya eṣaḥ sa jñastathā /
children.translated_text: <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower), <s>akṣara</s> (imperishable), <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath), 'who?', 'this one', 'he', the knower, likewise
<s>aja</s> (unborn)—these are the names in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> for that which is designated <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Thus:
One who knows the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, devoted to whatever stage of life,

children.text: muṇḍī jaṭī śikhī vāpi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: whether shaven-headed, wearing matted hair, or bearing a topknot—is liberated; there is no doubt about this.
Is this <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is beyond <s>prakṛti</s>, an agent or a non-agent?
If he were the agent of good and evil deeds, he would act without the three mental modifications (<s>vṛttis</s>);

body.translated_text: but if agency belongs to the qualities observed in the world, how can it be attributed [to <s>Puruṣa</s>]?

children.translated_text: From the association [of <s>Puruṣa</s> with <s>guṇas</s>], through <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, ritual bathing, and meditation—
the <s>sāttvic</s> modification manifests in the illumination of knowledge, sovereignty, and transformation.

children.text: rāgaḥ krodho lobhaḥ paraparivādo nindā tuṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Passion, anger, greed, disparagement of others, blame, [false] contentment,
distorted form, and harshness—this is well known as the <s>rājasic</s> intellect.
Madness, intoxication, despair, atheism, excessive attachment to women,
sleep, laziness, cruelty, and impurity—this is the <s>tāmasic</s> modification.
Seeing this threefold modification [as belonging to the <s>guṇas</s>], agency belongs to the <s>guṇas</s>;

children.text: akartā puruṣaḥ siddha iti siddhānta iṣyate //
children.translated_text: that <s>Puruṣa</s> is a non-agent is established—such is the accepted doctrine.
The one who, [observing] the <s>guṇas</s> of active <s>prakṛti</s>,
through the distorted perception [caused] by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>,
concealing the self, to himself
the ignorant one falsely conceives: 'I am the doer.'
Unable to hold even the tip of a hair on his belly,
he thought: 'All this was done by me.'
He behaves as though mad—such is ignorance.
Alas, O Creator, who is this one who presumes himself learned!
Thus it is stated in the <s>Gītā</s>:
'All actions are performed in every way by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>prakṛti</s>;
the one whose self is deluded by <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) thinks: "I am the doer."'
'Because of being beginningless and without qualities, this <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is imperishable;

children.text: śarīrastho 'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate //
children.translated_text: though dwelling in the body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, he neither acts nor is tainted.'

body.text:
prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ /
  yaḥ paśyati sadā '; 'tmānamakartāraṃ sa paśyati // ityādi /

children.text: sa ekaḥ puruṣaḥ kiṃ vā nāneti ca vicāraya /
children.translated_text: Now consider: is <s>Puruṣa</s> one, or many?
Because of the diversity of pleasure, pain, delusion, confusion, purification, birth, and death,
the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established from their multiplicity, and also from the distinctions of worlds, stages of life, and classes.

body.translated_text: 'Actions are performed in every way by <s>prakṛti</s> alone; he who always sees the self as a non-agent—he truly sees.' And so forth.

children.translated_text: If <s>Puruṣa</s> were one, the absurdity of loss of intellect would follow;

children.text: ekasmin sukhite sarve sukhinaḥ syurataḥ param /
children.translated_text: when one is happy, all would be happy; moreover,

children.text: ekasmin duḥkhite sarve duḥkhitāḥ syuriti kramāt //
children.translated_text: when one suffers, all would suffer—such would be the consequence.

body.text:
ato bahutvaṃ saṃsiddhaṃ bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ākṛtigarbhāśayabhāvasaṅgatiśarīravibhāgālliṅgabahutvāt sāṃkhyācāryāḥ kapilāsuripañcaśikhapatañjaliprabhṛtayaḥ puruṣabahutvaṃ varṇayanti |

children.text: vedavādina ācāryā hariharahiraṇyagarbhavyāsādaya ekamātmānaṃ, tathā ca śrutiḥ |
children.translated_text: the Vedic teachers—<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, and others—[hold] the self to be one. And thus the <s>Śruti</s> [says]:

children.text: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yadbhūtaṃ yacca bhāvyam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this—whatever has been and whatever will be;
he is the lord of immortality, who grows beyond through food.'
'That alone is <s>Agni</s>, that is <s>Āditya</s>, that is <s>Vāyu</s>, and that is <s>Candramās</s> (the moon);

body.translated_text: Therefore, plurality is fully established; <s>Puruṣas</s> are remembered as many—because of the multiplicity of forms, wombs, dispositions, temperaments, associations, and bodily divisions, and because of the multiplicity of subtle bodies. The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers—<s>Kapila</s>, <s>Āsuri</s>, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, <s>Patañjali</s>—

children.text: tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tā āpaḥ sa prajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: that alone is the bright one, that is <s>Brahman</s>, those are the waters, he is <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: tadeva satyamamṛtaṃ sa mokṣaḥ sā parā gatiḥ //
children.translated_text: that alone is truth, the immortal; he is liberation, that is the supreme goal.

children.text: tadakṣaraṃ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ yasmāt paraṃ nāparamasti kiñcit /
children.translated_text: That is the imperishable, that is the most excellent of <s>Savitṛ</s>, beyond which there is nothing higher nor anything else;
than which nothing is smaller and nothing greater.'

children.text: vṛkṣa iva stambho divi tiṣṭhatyekaḥ tenedaṃ pūrṇaṃ puruṣeṇa /
children.translated_text: Like a tree, like a pillar, He stands alone in heaven; by that <s>Puruṣa</s> this [universe] is filled.
Having hands and feet everywhere, having eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,
having ears everywhere in the world, He stands encompassing all.
Appearing to have the qualities of all senses, yet devoid of all senses,
the Lord (<s>Īśāna</s>) of all living beings, the great refuge of all,
[present] everywhere among all beings, the Self of all, the source of all.

children.text: sarvaṃ vilīyate yasmin tadbrahma munayo viduḥ /
children.translated_text: That in which all dissolves — the sages know that as <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: eka eva hi bhūtātmā bhūte bhūte vyavasthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Indeed, the one Self of all beings is established in each and every being.
He is seen as one and as many, like the moon [reflected] in water.

children.text: sa hi sarveṣu bhūteṣu sthāvareṣu careṣu ca //
children.translated_text: For He, in all beings, movable and immovable,

body.text: vasatyeko mahānātmā yena sarvamidaṃ tatam // ityādi /
body.translated_text: dwells as the one great Self, by whom all this is pervaded. Thus and so forth.
The three <s>guṇas</s> (<s>traiguṇya</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 4 ||

children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these are the <s>guṇas</s>; their triad constitutes <s>traiguṇya</s>.
Clarity, lightness, attachment, from attachment arises delight, and straightforwardness,
contentment, forbearance — these are the forms of <s>sattva</s>, directly bringing happiness.
Grief, stupefaction, hatred, affliction, weariness, indulgence, and conceit —
these are the many forms of <s>rajas</s>, which bring much suffering.
<s>Tamas</s> is characterized by obscuration and the like, loathsomeness, concealment, and such;
it has the characteristics of wretchedness, heaviness, sleep, heedlessness, and sloth.
It is of the nature of delusion and endless — thus the triad of <s>guṇas</s> has been declared.
One should know <s>sattva</s> as illuminating, <s>rajas</s> as activating,

body.text: vināśakaṃ tamo vidyāt traiguṇyaṃ nāma sañjñitam /
body.translated_text: and <s>tamas</s> as destructive — such is designated as the triad of <s>guṇas</s>.
Evolution (<s>saṃcara</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 5 ||

children.text: sāmyāvasthā guṇānāṃ yā prakṛtiḥ sā svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: That state of equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> — that is <s>Prakṛti</s> by its very nature.
Through the agitation of time, by disequilibrium, in the field conjoined with the Supreme, formerly —
from that [arose] <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and then <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense), threefold, was born.
The <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), the <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties), and the <s>mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements), in sequence —

body.translated_text: thus the origination in sequence is declared as <s>saṃcara</s> (evolution).
Involution (<s>pratisaṃcara</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 6 ||

children.translated_text: In reverse order, the five gross elements dissolve into the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements).
The <s>tanmātras</s> and the sense faculties dissolve into <s>ahaṅkāra</s>.
<s>Ahaṅkāra</s> [dissolves] then into <s>buddhi</s>, and <s>buddhi</s> into that called <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest).

children.text: avyaktaṃ na kvacillīnaṃ pratisañcara iti smṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>avyakta</s> does not dissolve anywhere — this is remembered as <s>pratisaṃcara</s> (involution).

body.translated_text: The subjective (<s>adhyātma</s>), the objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>), and the divine (<s>adhidaivata</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 7 ||

children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>manas</s> (mind), the ear, the skin, the two eyes,
the tongue, the nose, the feet, the anus, and the generative organ — these are designated as <s>adhyātma</s> (the subjective).

body.text:
yattu mokṣadharme
  ādau mana ahaṅkārāt jāyate vṛttayascatāḥ //
body.translated_text: However, in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> [it is said]: 'First, the mind is born from <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and from it [arise] the functions.'

children.translated_text: 'From the desire for sound, the ear is born for this being of cultivated nature;
likewise from the desire for form, the eye; and the nose from the desire to perceive smell.'

body.translated_text: Thus and so forth — the sense faculties arise as effects of desire and other functions of the mind; this should be understood as being in accordance with the <s>Vedānta</s> method. [Now,] <s>adhibhūta</s> (the objective):

children.translated_text: In their respective order: that which is to be cognized, that which is to be thought upon,
that which is to be imagined, that which is to be heard, that which is to be touched, that which is to be seen,
that which is to be tasted, that which is to be smelled, that which is to be walked upon, that which is to be excreted,
and that which is to be enjoyed — thus is <s>adhibhūta</s> (the objective domain) declared.
And the <s>adhidaivata</s> (the divine correlates):
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the Moon, Space, Wind,

children.text: sūryo varuṇa indraśca viṣṇumitraṃ tathaiva ca //
children.translated_text: the Sun, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Mitra</s> likewise —
He who knows the four [aspects] and how —
by means of each sense, their own natures and the corresponding deity,
freed from the contact of faults that have arisen [from past karma],

children.text: guṇāṃstu bhuṅkte na guṇaiḥ sa yujyate //
children.translated_text: he experiences the <s>guṇas</s> but is not bound by the <s>guṇas</s>.

body.translated_text: in this very order has the <s>adhidaivata</s> (divine correlation) been proclaimed.
The five cognitive faculties (<s>pañcābhibuddhi</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 8 ||

children.translated_text: The cognitive faculty characterized by desire should be understood through its orientation toward action:
'This is to be done by me' — this is determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>); 'I shall do it' —

children.text: icchā vāñchā 'tha saṅkalpo manasaḥ karma ceṣyate /
children.translated_text: desire, longing, and then volition — these are the actions of the mind.
Thus these five cognitive faculties have been fully declared.

body.translated_text: The five sources of action (<s>pañca karmayonayaḥ</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 9 ||

children.translated_text: Steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), desire for happiness (<s>sukhā</s>), desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>), and the absence of those two —
these five are generally enumerated as the sources of action.
The conviction that attaches itself to speech, action, and volition —
being devoted to that and established in that — this is the characteristic of steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>).
Freedom from jealousy, celibacy, performing sacrifice, officiating at sacrifice, austerity,
receiving gifts, and offering oblations — these are remembered as the characteristics of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>).

children.text: sukhaṃ sukhārthī seveta vidyā karma tapāṃsi ca /
children.translated_text: One who seeks happiness should cultivate: learning, action, and austerities,
being always devoted to expiation — this is declared as the [source called] desire for happiness (<s>sukhā</s>).
Like one stupefied by the fumes of poison, the desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) is the source of wisdom for meditators.

children.text: ekatvaṃ ca pṛthaktvaṃ ca nityaṃ vedamacetanam //
children.translated_text: Oneness and separateness, eternality, the <s>Veda</s>, and the non-conscious,
the subtle, the effect-in-cause doctrine (<s>satkārya</s>), and agitation — this should be known as <s>vividiṣā</s>.
<s>Vividiṣā</s> is the innate disposition (<s>prākṛtī vṛtti</s>) that makes one capable of [discriminating between] effect and cause.

children.text: dhṛtiḥ śraddhā vividiṣā sukhā ceti catuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: Steadfastness, faith, desire to know, and desire for happiness — these four
should be known [as sources of bondage, while] <s>vividiṣā</s> is designated for liberation.
This nature of the sources of action has been declared in detail.

body.translated_text: The five vital airs (<s>pañca vāyavaḥ</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 10 ||

children.text: prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaśca udāno vyāna eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s> —
these are the five vital airs in the bodies of embodied beings.
That which moves in the mouth and nose, and gives life — it is called <s>prāṇa</s>.
That which moves below the navel, carrying downward — it is regarded as <s>apāna</s>.
Because it governs the heart and distributes [nourishment] — it is called <s>samāna</s>.
Because it moves upward from the throat — it is remembered as <s>udāna</s>.

body.translated_text: <s>Vyāna</s> [is so called] because it is situated in the joints, and causes dispersal and expansion.
The five agents of action (<s>pañca karmātmānaḥ</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 11 ||

children.translated_text: The <s>vaikārika</s> (modified) and other [types] have been previously enumerated in order.
[They produce] auspicious, inauspicious, deluded, auspicious-deluded, and inauspicious-deluded [actions] —

body.translated_text: as agents [they perform] their respective actions in that order, it is declared.
The five-branched ignorance (<s>pañcaparva avidyā</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 12 ||
Darkness (<s>tamas</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), great delusion (<s>mahāmoha</s>), gloom (<s>tāmisra</s>), and blind darkness (<s>andhatāmisra</s>) —

children.translated_text: <s>tamas</s> and <s>moha</s> are each eightfold, based on the eightfold <s>Prakṛti</s>.
[Tamas is] the false identification with self-knowledge; [moha is] the conceit of lordship through attainment (<s>prāpti</s>) and the like.
Regarding the five sensory objects — both those directly perceived and those heard of —
the delusion that is ego-identification — that is <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), which is tenfold.
[The grief] regarding the eight lordships and ten [sensory] objects is called <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom).
That despair which arises at death is <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness).

body.translated_text: This five-branched ignorance is divided into sixty-two varieties.
The twenty-eight-fold disability (<s>aṣṭāviṃśatidhā aśakti</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 13 ||

children.translated_text: Dullness, leprosy, hunchbackedness, deformity, loss of smell, muteness, lameness,

children.text: kuṇirgudāvartti ca ṣaṇḍhatā ca unmāda ityeṣa nirūpito 'yam //
children.translated_text: having a withered arm, prolapse of the rectum, impotence, and madness — thus have these been described.
The destruction of the eleven sense faculties, characterized by deafness and the like —
and the destruction of <s>buddhi</s> [constitutes] seventeen [varieties]: the inversions of contentment and perfection.
The conviction that '<s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) does not exist' — this is [the first inverse called] <s>ajambhikā</s>.
'The <s>Mahat</s> does not exist' — this is <s>asalilā</s>; 'there is no seeking' and 'there is no <s>ahaṅkāra</s>' [are the next].
'There is no unseen [merit]' [is another], and [the denial that] the five <s>tanmātras</s> are the cause of the elements.
'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' — being <s>Brahman</s>, one attains <s>Brahman</s>.
Just as [this is the view] of the <s>Vedāntins</s>, so is such the view of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>.
<s>Asutā</s> (joyless contentment) is activity in acquiring sense objects;
<s>sutarā</s> is excessive activity in protecting [what is acquired];
activity in wealth without seeing the fault of [its] cost —
<s>asunetrā</s> — thus is it declared by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>.
<s>Akurmarīcikā</s> — the incapacity for enjoyment of one who does not see [the fault of] violence and the like;
<s>anuttambhā</s> and <s>ambhasikā</s> — the engaging in enjoyment through deception due to fault.
These have been described as ninefold; therein the inversions of contentment —
the eight perfections (<s>siddhis</s>) are described; those are the inversions of perfection.
For one whose mind is deluded by multiplicity, the perfection of oneness is <s>tārakam</s> (the saving [knowledge]);
wrong apprehension from hearing [mere] words — that is <s>asutārakam</s>.

children.text: nānātvajño mukta iti śrutvaikajño na muktibhāk /
children.translated_text: Having heard that the knower of multiplicity is liberated, the knower of oneness does not attain liberation —
not saving [from <s>saṃsāra</s>] due to ignorance and devotion to false scriptures.
Even for one who suffers, the absence of agitation — that is <s>apramodā</s> in <s>saṃsāra</s>.
<s>Apramuda</s> — or that which is falsely delighted through ignorance, or false delight —
from incorrect speech or from obstruction toward the teacher.

children.text: abhāgyasya na siddhiḥ syāt jñāne tat samudīritam /
children.translated_text: For the unfortunate one there is no perfection in knowledge — that is declared.
From association with the attached, the ignorance that follows knowledge — that is <s>aramyakam</s> (unpleasant).
Thus explained in the earlier manner are these eight inversions of perfection (<s>siddhiviparyaya</s>).
The twenty-eight-fold disability has been explained through the combination of both [types].

body.translated_text: The ninefold contentment (<s>navadhā tuṣṭi</s>). || <s>Tattva</s> 14 ||
By accepting that <s>Prakṛti</s> itself is the Supreme Self, one becomes a possessor of [false] contentment.

children.translated_text: [When one] resorts to indifference — that contentment is called <s>ambhas</s> (water).

children.text: buddhau ca paramātmatve tuṣṭiḥ sā salilā smṛtā //
children.translated_text: Contentment in [regarding] <s>buddhi</s> as the Supreme Self — that is known as <s>salilā</s> (fluid).

children.text: ahaṃkāre yadā sā syādāyācchā iti śabdhitā /
children.translated_text: When that [contentment] is in [regarding] <s>ahaṅkāra</s> [as supreme] — it is termed <s>āyācchā</s>.
When that contentment is in the <s>tanmātras</s> — it is called <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (sight).
These four internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) contentments indeed arise.
Even in these there is no liberation; [liberation comes] from knowledge of reality (<s>tattva</s>) as taught.
In acquiring wealth there is suffering, and in protecting what is acquired;

children.text: tyāge duḥkhaṃ kṣaye duḥkhaṃ dhigarthaṃ duḥkhabhājanam // iti
children.translated_text: in renouncing there is suffering, in loss there is suffering — shame on wealth, the vessel of sorrow! Thus [it is said].
One who is content through seeing the faults [of wealth] — [by knowing] the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone — attains liberation.
This fifth <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) called <s>sutā</s> [arises] from the absence of knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) and so forth. //
The sixth, <s>sutarā</s>, [arises] from [contentment in] protection; the seventh, from the perception of decay;
<s>Sunetrā</s>, the eighth, [arises] from the fault of attachment, [also called] <s>kurmarīcikā</s> (mirage). //
From faults such as violence in [pursuit of] objects, there is withdrawal (<s>nivṛtti</s>), and [this ninth is called] <s>samaskarī</s>;
The ninth <s>tuṣṭi</s> is declared [to be called] <s>uttamāmbhasikā</s> ('of the highest water'). //

body.translated_text: The <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) is eightfold. || <s>Tats</s>_15 ||

children.text: jñānaṃ yaddūramutpannaṃ tārākhyā prathamā hi sā /
children.translated_text: The knowledge that arises from afar — that is the first, called <s>tārā</s>;
Knowledge [arising] merely from hearing words among beings is considered <s>sutārā</s>. //
Knowledge through study itself — the third is [called] <s>tārayantī</s> ('that which causes to cross');
From the removal of <s>ādhyātmika</s> (inner) suffering, [the fourth] is called <s>pramodā</s> ('joy'). //
From the removal of <s>bhautika</s> (physical/elemental) affliction, the <s>siddhi</s> called <s>pramudā</s> ('delight') is stated;
From the removal of <s>ādhidaivika</s> (supernatural) affliction, knowledge arises in humans. //
The sixth <s>siddhi</s> of the virtuous is called <s>pramodamānā</s> ('exulting'), by its own nature;
From the destruction of attachment to pleasant company, the seventh is known as <s>ramyakā</s> ('delightful'). //
The eighth <s>siddhi</s> is <s>pramudā</s> (supreme delight), [arising] from service to the <s>guru</s> and so forth;
Thus these eight <s>siddhis</s>, which are the means to knowledge, have been explained. //

body.translated_text: The ten fundamental topics (<s>mūlikārthas</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_16 ||

children.translated_text: Existence, oneness, having a true purpose,
being-for-another, otherness, non-agentship,
conjunction (<s>yoga</s>), disjunction (<s>viyoga</s>), the multiplicity of souls (<s>pumāṃsaḥ</s>),
the persistence of the body, and residual activity (<s>śeṣavṛtti</s>). //
This is the enumeration of the ten fundamental topics (<s>daśamūlikā</s>): from the fact of being-an-aggregate and being-for-another,
the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s> is established; from transformation, the cause of difference;
that the <s>Avyakta</s> (unmanifest) exists, is infinite, is one — and [Puruṣa's nature is] beyond attachment and sorrow,
the otherness [of Puruṣa] is established from the multiplicity of purposes [served] for another and from the three <s>guṇas</s>. //
Non-agentship [is established] from the reversal [of misidentification]; conjunction (<s>yoga</s>) is from the vision of <s>Puruṣa</s>;
when the separation of the body occurs, from the perception of having fulfilled one's purpose, //
they are known as multiple, from the difference [in] causes beginning with birth and ending with instruments;
like the turning of a wheel, residual activity [continues]. These are the ten established fundamental topics. //
Previously taught by the <s>Saptati</s> (Sāṃkhyakārikā), these fifty categories (<s>pratyayas</s>)
together with sixty topics — thus it is called the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> ('Treatise of Sixty [Topics]'). //

body.translated_text: The creation for the sake of benefit (<s>anugrahasarga</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_17 ||

children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> created [the world as a] favor (<s>anugraha</s>), separately from <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form-subtle-element),
having produced [beings] through meditation for [their] benefit, [free] from the previous material support. //

body.translated_text: The creation of beings is of fourteen kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_18 ||

children.translated_text: The divine is of eight kinds: <s>paiśāca</s> (of <s>piśācas</s>), <s>rākṣasa</s> (of <s>rākṣasas</s>), likewise

<s>gāndharva</s> (of <s>gandharvas</s>), <s>aindra</s> (of <s>Indra</s>'s realm), <s>brāhma</s> (of <s>Brahmā</s>), and <s>saumya</s> (of <s>Soma</s>) — these eight belong to the <s>brāhma</s> [category]. //
These are the divine classes of beings; the animal kingdom (<s>tiryagyoni</s>) is of five kinds:
wild animals, domestic animals, birds, reptiles, and immobile beings — thus distinguished by their divisions. //
The human kind is of one type, from <s>brāhmaṇas</s> down to <s>cāṇḍālas</s>;
domestic animals [range] from cows to mice; birds from <s>Garuḍa</s> onward; //
wild animals from mosquitoes onward and from lions to jackals;
serpents from <s>Śeṣa</s> to water-snakes; and mountains, earth, and grasses //

body.translated_text: are the immobile beings. [This is] the elemental creation — this is the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>. //
Bondage is of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_19 ||

children.translated_text: <s>Prākṛtibandha</s> (bondage of <s>Prakṛti</s>) is dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>, from identifying with the supreme;
for <s>saṃnyāsins</s>, dissolution into the senses is the other, <s>vaikārika</s> (transformative) [bondage]. //
For householders, <s>dakṣiṇā</s>-bondage [belongs to] those who pride themselves on generosity;
thus this threefold bondage [is described]; threefold liberation is [now] stated. //

body.translated_text: Liberation is of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_20 ||

children.translated_text: From the abundance of knowledge and from cessation [of activity], the destruction of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> occurs;
from the destruction of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation) is proclaimed. //
It has been said:

children.text: ādyo hi mokṣo jñānena dvitīyo rāgasaṃkṣayāt /
children.translated_text: The first liberation is through knowledge; the second from the destruction of attachment;
the third from the complete destruction [of all bonds] — thus the characteristics of <s>mokṣa</s> have been explained. //

body.translated_text: The valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) are threefold. || <s>Tats</s>_21 ||

children.translated_text: Perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and the word of an authority (<s>āptavacana</s>) — these are the valid means of knowledge;
the five sense organs constitute direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>); [that] rain [follows] from the appearance of clouds //

body.translated_text: is inference (<s>anumāna</s>); '<s>Indra</s> is the king of the gods' — [this authoritative] word is a valid means of knowledge. //
In scripture (<s>āgama</s>) also [it is said]: 'One who is liberated by one's own actions, free from desire and aversion, //
possessed of knowledge and endowed with good conduct — such a one should be known as [an authority].' //
Suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) is threefold. || <s>Tats</s>_22 ||

children.translated_text: Suffering is declared to be threefold: <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to beings),

children.text: ādhidaivaṃ ca tatrāpi prathamaṃ dvividhaṃ smṛtam //
children.translated_text: and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to fate/gods). Of these, the first is known to be twofold: //
bodily and mental — arising from disorders of <s>vāta</s> (wind), desire, and so forth;
that which arises from beings such as humans and others is <s>ādhibhautika</s>; //
that arising from gods, cold, wind, and so forth is <s>ādhidaivika</s>;
this has been stated in brief — the explanation of the <s>sūtras</s> according to [our] understanding. //

body.translated_text: And I shall now explain the procedure for the benefit of followers of the <s>Purāṇas</s>. //
This is the authentic tradition passed down in succession. || <s>Tats</s>_23 ||

body.text: etat sarvaṃ jñātvā kṛtakṛtyaḥ syāt || Tats_24 ||
body.translated_text: Having known all this, one becomes one who has accomplished what is to be accomplished. || <s>Tats</s>_24 ||
One is no longer overcome by the threefold suffering. || <s>Tats</s>_25 ||

body.text:
mahān ahaṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇi avyaktasaṃjñāni bhavanti mahacchabdena hairaṇyagarbho buddhirucyate |
pradhānaṃ mūlamavyaktasaṃjñam |
jñaḥ puruṣaḥ |
etāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni |
tatra pradhānaṃ kāraṇameva na kāryam |
mahadādayaḥ sapta pūrvapūrvasya kāryāṇi uttarottarasya kāraṇāni |
indriyāṇyekādaśa pañca mahābhūtāni kāryāṇyeva na kāraṇāni |

children.text: puruṣastu na kāryaṃ na vā kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s>, however, is neither an effect nor a cause.
As stated [in the kārikā]: 'The root <s>Prakṛti</s>...' and so forth.

children.text: mahān ahaṃkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇi sapta prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, and the five <s>tanmātras</s> — [these] seven are both <s>prakṛtis</s> (causes) and <s>vikṛtis</s> (effects).

children.text: pradhānād buddhirjāyata iti pradhānavikāraḥ saivāhaṅkāraṃ janayatīti prakṛtiḥ ahaṅkāro 'pi buddherjāyata iti vikṛtiḥ so 'pi ekādaśendriyāṇi pañca tanmātrāṇi janayatīti prakṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>buddhi</s> is born — hence it is a modification (<s>vikāra</s>) of <s>Pradhāna</s>. That same [buddhi] generates <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> — hence it is a <s>prakṛti</s> (productive cause). <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> too, being born from <s>buddhi</s>, is a <s>vikṛti</s>; and it also generates the eleven sense organs and the five <s>tanmātras</s> — hence it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. ||

body.translated_text: <s>Mahat</s> (the Great), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — these are called <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest). By the term '<s>mahat</s>', the <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — is meant. <s>Pradhāna</s>, the root, bears the designation <s>avyakta</s>. The knower is <s>Puruṣa</s>. These are the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles). Among them, <s>Pradhāna</s> is a cause only, not an effect. <s>Mahat</s> and the [next] seven are effects of each preceding [principle] and causes of each succeeding one. The eleven sense organs and the five gross elements are effects only, not causes.

body.text: tatra śabdatanamātramahaṃkārājjāyata iti vikṛtistasmādākāśaṃ jāyata iti śabdatanmātraṃ prakṛtiḥ |

children.text: tathā sparśatanmātramahaṃkārājjāyata iti vikṛtiḥ tadeva vāyuṃ janayatīti prakṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch-subtle-element) is born from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> — hence a <s>vikṛti</s>; that same [tanmātra] generates <s>vāyu</s> (air) — hence it is a <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: evaṃ rūpatanmātramahaṃkārājjāyata iti vikṛtiḥ tadeva tejo janayatīti prakṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Similarly, <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form-subtle-element) is born from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> — hence a <s>vikṛti</s>; that same [tanmātra] generates <s>tejas</s> (fire) — hence it is a <s>prakṛti</s>.
<s>Rasa-tanmātra</s> (taste-subtle-element) is born from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> — hence a <s>vikṛti</s>; that same [tanmātra] generates water (<s>ambhas</s>) — hence it is a <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: tathā gandhatanmātramahaṃkārājjāyata iti vikṛtiḥ tadevāvaniṃ janayatīti prakṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> (smell-subtle-element) is born from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> — hence a <s>vikṛti</s>; that same [tanmātra] generates earth (<s>avanī</s>) — hence it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. ||

body.translated_text: Among them, <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound-subtle-element) is born from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> — hence a <s>vikṛti</s>; from it <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is born — hence <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> is a <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: etāni pañca tanmātrāṇi sūkṣmabhūtāni sthūlabhūtānāṃ kāraṇāni ṣoḍaśakaśca vikāraḥ |
children.translated_text: These five <s>tanmātras</s> are the subtle elements — the causes of the gross elements — and the sixteen-fold group of modifications (<s>vikāra</s>).

children.text: pañca buddhīndriyāṇi pañca karmendriyāṇi ekādaśaṃ manaḥ pañca mahābhūtāni eṣa ṣoḍaśako gaṇo vikāra eva na prakṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: The five cognitive sense organs (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>), the five action organs (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>), the eleventh being mind (<s>manas</s>), and the five gross elements (<s>mahābhūtāni</s>) — this group of sixteen is modification only, not a productive cause.
But <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither [cause nor effect] — this is the meaning. ||

body.text:
pratyakṣānumānaśabdarūpaṃ trividhaṃ pramāṇam |
tatra pratyakṣaṃ tāvat śrotrādipañcakaṃ lokocitaśabdādiguṇagrāhakam |

children.translated_text: Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) apprehends objects not directly perceived, [as] through smoke and the like.

children.text: śabdastāvat trividho bhavati vāgindriyaviṣayaḥ śrotraviṣayo buddhimātraviṣayaśca |
children.translated_text: Verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is of three kinds: it is the object of the speech-organ, the object of the ear, and the object of the intellect alone.

children.text: teṣu kaṇṭhatālvādisthalāvacchinnaḥ śabdo vāgīndriyaviṣayaḥ tatkāryatvāt vāgindriyavyavahitaśrotrasthaśca śabdataḥ śabdaḥ śrotrasya viṣayastadgrāhyatvāt |
children.translated_text: Among these, the sound delimited by the places of articulation such as throat, palate, and so forth is the object of the speech-organ, because it is produced by the speech-organ; and the sound [arising] from that sound, reaching the ear through the intermediary of the speech-organ, is the object of the ear, because it is apprehended by it.

children.text: ghaṭa ityādipadāni tu buddhimātrasya viṣayaḥ vakṣyamāṇayuktyā buddhimātragrāhyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: But words such as 'pot' and the like are the object of the intellect alone, because they are apprehended only by the intellect, as will be explained by the reasoning [to follow]. ||

body.translated_text: The threefold <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) consists of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). Among these, perception is the fivefold [group of] sense organs beginning with hearing, which apprehend qualities such as sound and so forth as known in ordinary experience.

body.text:
tāni padānyevārthasya karaṇatvāt sphoṭa ityucyate |
taddi padaṃ vāgindriyoccāryapratyekavarṇebhyo 'tiriktaṃ varṇānāmāśutaravināśitayā melanābhāvenaikaṃ padamiti vyavahāragocaratvāsambhavāt arthasmārakatvāsambhavācca |
asya ca sphoṭasya kāraṇamekaḥ prayatnaviśeṣaḥ prayatnabhedenoccāraṇe sati ekapadavyavahārābhāvādarthāpratyayācca tasya ca sphoṭasya vyañjaka ānupūrvīviśiṣṭatayā antyavarṇapratyayaḥ ataśca buddhereva sphoṭagrāhakatvam ānupūrvyā buddhyaiva grahaṇasambhavena sāmānādhikaraṇyapratyāsattyaivānupūrvīpratyayasya sphoṭākhyapadābhivyaktihetutve lāghavāt |
ata eva sphoṭaḥ śrotreṇa grahītuṃ na śakyate ghottaraṭatvādirarūpiṇyā ānupūrvyāḥ śrotreṇa grahaṇāsambhavāt āśutaravināśitayā varṇānāṃ melanāsambhavāt pūrvapūrvavarṇasaṃskārāṇāṃ tatsmṛtīnāṃ cāntaḥkaraṇaniṣṭhānāmantaḥkaraṇasahakāritvasyaivaucityāditi |
body.translated_text: Those very words, because they are the instruments of [communicating] meaning, are called <s>sphoṭa</s>. That word is distinct from the individual phonemes uttered by the speech-organ, because — due to the rapid destruction of phonemes — their combination is impossible, and therefore being an object of the convention 'this is one word' is impossible, as is the capacity to remind [one] of meaning. The cause of this <s>sphoṭa</s> is a single specific effort [of the speaker], because in the absence of a difference in effort there would be no convention of [recognizing] a single word and no cognition of meaning. The revealer of that <s>sphoṭa</s> is the cognition of the final phoneme qualified by the particular sequence; therefore the intellect alone is the apprehender of <s>sphoṭa</s>, since the apprehension of the sequence is possible by the intellect alone, and by co-reference and proximity alone, the cognition of the sequence is the cause of the manifestation of the word called <s>sphoṭa</s> — this being more parsimonious. Therefore <s>sphoṭa</s> cannot be apprehended by the ear, because the sequence — which is formless, consisting of [sounds] like 'gho' followed by 'ṭa' — cannot be apprehended by the ear, because the combination of rapidly-perishing phonemes is impossible, and because the impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) of the preceding phonemes and the memories [they produce], being located in the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), are fittingly auxiliaries of the inner organ alone.

children.text: syādetat sphoṭavyañjakasyānupūrvīviśiṣṭacaramavarṇasyaiva padatvamarthapratyāyakatvaṃ vā 'stu alaṃ sphoṭena taddhetoreva tadastviti nyāyāt |
children.translated_text: One might object: let the final phoneme qualified by the specific sequence, which is the revealer of <s>sphoṭa</s>, itself be the word, or let it [itself] be the communicator of meaning — what need is there for <s>sphoṭa</s>? — [for] by the maxim 'when the cause itself suffices, let it be [the explanation].'

children.text: etadeva sāṃkhyasūtreṇoktaṃ pratītyapratītibhyāṃ na sphoṭātmakaḥ śabda iti |
children.translated_text: This very point is stated by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Śabda</s> (word) is not of the nature of <s>sphoṭa</s>, because of cognition and non-cognition.'
The cognition of unity is also explained as being the unity of the final letter qualified by sequence.
If so, the consequence would be the annihilation of the <s>avayavin</s> (whole).

children.text: asamavāyikāraṇasaṃyogaviśeṣāvacchinnānāmavayavānāmeva jalādyāharaṇahetutvakalpanāyāṃ lāghavāt taddhetoreva tadastviti nyāyasāmyāt eko ghaṭa ityādipratyayānāmapyekaṃ vanamityādipratyayavadupapatteḥ |
children.translated_text: Since in supposing that the parts themselves — delimited by the specific conjunctions that are their non-inherent causes — are the cause of fetching water and such, there is parsimony, and since the reasoning is equal in saying 'let that very cause of that suffice,' cognitions such as 'one pot' are also explained just like cognitions such as 'one forest.'

children.text: atha paramāṇūnāṃ tatsaṃyogānāṃ cātīndriyatayā tadrūpatve 'vayavinaḥ pratyakṣānupapattirityādikamavayavisādhakamiti cet tulyaṃ sphoṭe 'pi ānupūrvyāḥ kṣaṇādyatīndriyaghaṭitatayā ānupūrvīviśiṣṭacaramavarṇātmakatve padasya pratyakṣānupapattirityādikaṃ sphoṭasādhakamiti |
children.translated_text: Now, if it be argued that because atoms and their specific conjunctions are imperceptible, the direct perception of a whole possessing that nature would be impossible — and such arguments establish the parts — then the same applies equally to <s>sphoṭa</s>: since the sequence is composed of momentary and other imperceptible elements, if the word has the nature of the final letter qualified by sequence, the impossibility of direct perception and such arguments would equally establish <s>sphoṭa</s>.

children.text: api ca sphoṭaśabdo 'smābhiḥ śrutipramāṇenaiva svargādivat kalpyate ityatastatra laukikapramāṇābhāve 'pi na kṣatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, the word <s>sphoṭa</s> is postulated by us only on the authority of <s>Śruti</s> (scripture), just like heaven and the like; therefore, even in the absence of empirical proof, there is no harm.

body.translated_text: To this it is replied:

children.text: tathāhi praṇavasyākārokāramakārarūpamātrātrayaṃ brahmādidevatātrayātmakamuktvā praṇavaṃ devatātrayātiriktaparabrahmātmakaṃ caturthamātrāṃ śrutaya āmananti |
children.translated_text: For the <s>Śrutis</s> teach that <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) consists of the three <s>mātrās</s> (measures) in the form of the letters a, u, and m, having the three deities <s>Brahmā</s> and the others as their essence, and then declare the <s>Praṇava</s> as the fourth <s>mātrā</s>, whose essence is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> distinct from the three deities.

children.text: sā caturthī mātrā varṇatrayādatiriktaḥ sphoṭa eva sambhavati saiva cārddhamātretyucyate rāśivadavibhaktayorvarṇapadayorvarṇā ekamarddhaṃ padaṃ cānyadarddhamityupapadyate |
children.translated_text: That fourth <s>mātrā</s> can only be the <s>sphoṭa</s> which is distinct from the three letters; and that very [<s>mātrā</s>] is called the half-<s>mātrā</s> (<s>ardhamātrā</s>). Like a heap, of the undivided letter and word, the letters constitute one half, and the word constitutes the other half — thus it is explained.

children.text: yathā cāvayavebhyo vivicyāvayavī na vyavahāryo bhavati evameva pratyekavarṇebhyo vivicya padamuccārayituṃ na śakyata iti |
children.translated_text: Just as the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) cannot be employed in usage when separated from its parts, in exactly the same way the word cannot be pronounced when separated from its individual letters.

children.text: ataḥ smaryate "arddhamātrā sthitā nityā yānuccāryā viśeṣata" iti ||
children.translated_text: Hence it is remembered: 'The half-<s>mātrā</s> (<s>ardhamātrā</s>) abides eternally, which cannot be specifically pronounced.'
But what is the nature of <s>nāda</s> (resonance) and <s>bindu</s> (point)?

children.text: praṇave uccāryamāṇe śaṅkhanādaveṇunādādivadyaḥ svaraviśeṣo bhavati sa nādaḥ yā ca nādasyoparamāvasthā atisūkṣmā sā śūnyatulyatayā bindurucyata iti |
children.translated_text: When the <s>Praṇava</s> is being pronounced, the particular modulation of sound that arises — like the sound of a conch, the sound of a flute, and so forth — that is <s>nāda</s>; and the final state of cessation of that <s>nāda</s>, being extremely subtle, is called <s>bindu</s> because it resembles the void.

children.text: tasmādavayavebhyo 'vayavīva varṇebhyo 'tiriktaṃ padaṃ tadeva sphoṭa iti siddham |
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is distinct from its parts, the word (<s>pada</s>) is distinct from the letters — and that very [word] is the <s>sphoṭa</s>. This is established.

children.text: nanvevaṃ vākyamapi sphoṭaḥ syāditi cenna bādhakābhāve satīṣyatāmiti dik ||
children.translated_text: If it be objected that in this way even a sentence would be a <s>sphoṭa</s> — no, [we say] in the absence of any defeating argument, let it be accepted. This is the general direction [of the argument].

body.translated_text: Now, let this explanation of the half-<s>mātrā</s> be granted.

body.text:
śabdastāvat yathodeṣṭṛpuruṣavākyalakṣaṇaḥ indro devarāḍityādiḥ |
arthāpattisambhavābhāvaitihyapratibhopamānāni yadi pramāṇāni tarhyatraivāntarbhāvyāni na pṛthak |
prakṛtipuruṣau vidyamānāvapi nopalabhyete sūkṣmatvāt yathākāśe dhūmoṣmanīhāraparamāṇavaḥ santo 'pi nopalabhyante |
mahadādikāryadarśanena tatkāraṇamiva pradhānamanumīyate |
triguṇapradhānajanyaṃ mahadādikāryaṃ kiñcitprakṛtisadṛśaṃ kiñcidvikṛtisadṛśaṃ loke ubhayathā puttrarūpakāryadarśanāt |
tacca kāryaṃ sat nāsat na sadasat nānirvacanīyam atyantāsattve sikatābhyo 'pi tailamutpadyeta |
anyau ca pakṣau viruddhāveva avyaktasañjñaṃ pradhānaṃ svatantraṃ vyāpi nityaṃ ca vyaktasañjñaṃ kāryamasvatantramavyāpi anityaṃ ca |
puruṣaḥ svatantro vyāpī nityaśca |
trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ kāraṇaṃ pradhānaṃ taccaikaṃ lāghavāt |
pralayakāle mahadādikāryaṃ pradhāne līyate |
tacca pradhānaṃ sattvarajastamomayam |
guṇatrayasāmyāvasthā prakṛtiḥ |
pradhānamacetanaṃ puruṣastu cetanaḥ |
vyaktapradhānavilakṣaṇaḥ śuddho guṇarahitaḥ |
kāryasya sukhaduḥkhamohajanakatvena tatra kāraṇībhūtāni sattvarajastamāṃsi anumeyāni |

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ ca yathākramaṃ bhartṛsapatnīviṭeṣu sukhaduḥkhamohajanakatvaṃ kāminyāḥ |
children.translated_text: And it is observed that a woman produces, respectively, pleasure, pain, and delusion in her husband, co-wife, and paramour.

children.text: triguṇamaye 'pi kārye yadā sattvamudriktaṃ bhavati janādṛṣṭāt tadā rajastamasī abhibhūya svakāryaṃ sukhaṃ janayati |
children.translated_text: Even though the effect is constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, when <s>sattva</s> becomes predominant — due to the individual's <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) — it overpowers <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> and produces its own effect, namely pleasure.

children.text: evaṃ yadā raja udriktaṃ bhavati tadā sattvatamasī abhibhūya svakāryaṃ janayati duḥkham |
children.translated_text: Likewise, when <s>rajas</s> becomes predominant, it overpowers <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> and produces its own effect, namely pain.

children.text: evaṃ yadā tama udriktaṃ bhavati tadā sattvarajasī abhibhūya svakāryaṃ mohaṃ janayati ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, when <s>tamas</s> becomes predominant, it overpowers <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> and produces its own effect, namely delusion.

body.translated_text: The word (<s>śabda</s>), for its part, is as described — being in the form of the statement of the teaching authority, such as '<s>Indra</s> is the king of the gods,' and so forth. If <s>arthāpatti</s> (postulation), <s>sambhava</s> (subsumption), <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence), <s>aitihya</s> (tradition), <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition), and <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) are valid means of knowledge, they should be subsumed here itself, not counted separately. <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness), though existing, are not perceived due to their subtlety — just as smoke, heat, mist, and atoms, though present in space, are not perceived. Through the observation of effects such as <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) and the rest, their cause, namely <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), is inferred. The effects beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, born from the three-<s>guṇa</s> <s>Pradhāna</s>, are partly similar to the primary cause and partly similar to the modification — since in the world, from observing the effect in the form of a son's appearance, both [kinds of resemblance] are seen. And that effect is existent — not non-existent, not both existent and non-existent, and not indescribable; for if there were absolute non-existence, then oil could be extracted even from sand. The other two positions are contradictory. That which bears the name 'unmanifest' (<s>avyakta</s>) — <s>Pradhāna</s> — is independent, all-pervading, and eternal; while that which bears the name 'manifest' (<s>vyakta</s>) — the effect — is dependent, non-pervading, and non-eternal. <s>Puruṣa</s> is independent, all-pervading, and eternal. The cause of the three worlds is <s>Pradhāna</s>, and that is one, due to parsimony. At the time of dissolution, the effects beginning with <s>Mahat</s> dissolve into <s>Pradhāna</s>. And that <s>Pradhāna</s> is composed of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. The state of equilibrium of the three <s>guṇas</s> is <s>Prakṛti</s>. <s>Pradhāna</s> is non-conscious, while <s>Puruṣa</s> is conscious — distinct from the manifest and from <s>Pradhāna</s>, pure, devoid of <s>guṇas</s>. Since effects produce pleasure, pain, and delusion, the <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> that constitute their causes are to be inferred.

body.text:
duḥkhaṃ trividham ādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikabhedāt |
tathāhi tatra ādhyātmikaṃ dvirūpaṃ śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ceti |
śārīraṃ tāvat vātapittaśleṣmaviparyayakṛtaṃ jvarātīsārādi |
mānasaṃ tu priyaviyogāpriyasaṃyogādijam |
ādhibhautikaṃ tu caturddhābhūtagrāmanimittaṃ paśupakṣimṛgamanuṣyasarīsṛpadaṃśayūkāmatkuṇasthāvarebhyo jarāyujāṇḍajasvedajodbhijjebhyo jāyate |
divaḥ prabhavati taddaivaṃ tadadhikṛtya yajjāyate tadādhidaivikaṃ śītoṣṇavātavarṣāśanipātajam |
samuditatantavaḥ paṭamiva guṇasamudāyātmakaṃ pradhānam mahadādikāryaṃ janayati |
ekarasamapi yathā ākāśasalilaṃ vāpyādau patitaṃ sat vāpyādisaṃśleṣāt rasāntaramāpadyate tathā ekarūpādapi pradhānāddevādayaḥ krameṇa sukhino duḥkhino atyantamūḍhāśca bhavanti |
tathā sattvautkaṭyādrajastamasoraudāsīnyāddevāḥ atyantaṃ sukhinaḥ |
rajasa autkaṭyāt sattvatamasoraudāsīnyānmanuṣyāḥ atyantaṃ duḥkhinaḥ |
tamasa autkaṭyāt sattvarajasoraudāsīnyāttiryañcaḥ atyantaṃ mūḍhāḥ |
mahadādisaṅghātaḥ bhoktṛsāpekṣaḥ bhogyatvāt paryaṅkavat |
mahadādisaṅghaḥ parādhīnaḥ acetanatvāt mālāvat |
evaṃ puruṣo 'numīyate |
sa ca nānā janmamaraṇakaraṇānāṃ pratyekaṃ bhedāt |
ayamarthaḥ |
ekasya maraṇe sarve mriyeran yadyeka eva ātmā syāt ekasya ca janmani sarve jāyeran ekasya karaṇavaikalye sarve karaṇavaikalyavantaḥ syuḥ |
na caivaṃ dṛśyate tasmānnānā |
pañcaviṃśatitattvagocarasamyagjñānāt puruṣasya kaivalyaṃ bhavati |
taccānyatvaṃ pradhānādibheda iti yāvat |

children.translated_text: From non-discrimination comes <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage); from discrimination comes <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation).
In essence, the <s>akhyātivāda</s> (doctrine of non-apprehension) is accepted [by the Sāṃkhya school].

children.text: ata eva idaṃ rajatamiti jñānaṃ na bhramaḥ kiṃtu svarūpataḥ arthataśca aviviktaṃ jñānadvayam |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the cognition 'this is silver' is not an error, but rather a pair of cognitions that are undiscriminated both in their own nature and in their object.

children.text: yasya yādṛśamidaṃ rajatamiti rajatajñānaviṣayībhūtaṃ tasya tādṛśameva jagaditi nirṇayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is: for whomever the silver-cognition has such a content as 'this is silver,' for that person the world is of exactly the same nature.

body.translated_text: Suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) is threefold, by the distinction of <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to beings), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to the divine). As follows: the <s>ādhyātmika</s> is of two kinds — bodily and mental. The bodily is that caused by the derangement of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), such as fever, dysentery, and the like. The mental is that born from separation from the beloved, contact with the unwanted, and so forth. The <s>ādhibhautika</s> is of four kinds, caused by [various] classes of beings — it arises from domestic animals, birds, wild beasts, humans, snakes, mosquitoes, lice, bedbugs, and plants, from those born from wombs, eggs, moisture, and sprouting. That which originates from heaven is divine; that which is produced in relation to divinely caused [forces] is <s>ādhidaivika</s> — born from cold, heat, wind, rain, and lightning. Just as assembled threads produce a cloth, <s>Pradhāna</s>, whose nature is an aggregate of <s>guṇas</s>, generates the effects beginning with <s>Mahat</s>. Just as water of uniform taste in the sky, having fallen into a reservoir, acquires a different taste through contact with the reservoir, so too from <s>Pradhāna</s>, though of a single nature, the gods and others successively become happy, suffering, or extremely deluded. Thus, due to the predominance of <s>sattva</s> and the neutrality of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, the gods are supremely happy. Due to the predominance of <s>rajas</s> and the neutrality of <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, humans are supremely afflicted with suffering. Due to the predominance of <s>tamas</s> and the neutrality of <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>, animals are supremely deluded. The aggregate beginning with <s>Mahat</s> requires an experiencer, since it is something to be experienced — like a couch. The aggregate beginning with <s>Mahat</s> is dependent on another, since it is non-conscious — like a garland. Thus <s>Puruṣa</s> is inferred. And that [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is many, because of the distinctness of birth, death, and sense organs for each individual. The meaning is this: if there were only one <s>Ātman</s> (self), then upon the death of one, all would die; upon the birth of one, all would be born; upon the impairment of one's sense organs, all would have impaired sense organs. But this is not observed; therefore [<s>Puruṣas</s>] are many. From the correct knowledge pertaining to the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (categories), the <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) of <s>Puruṣa</s> occurs. And that [liberation] consists in the distinctness from <s>Pradhāna</s> and the rest.

body.text:
ata eva vastutastāttviko 'nyathābhāvaḥ pariṇāma ityeva lakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ pariṇāmo 'ṅgākṛtaḥ sa ca puruṣaḥ pratiśarīraṃ nānetyatrādi sma avikāritvāt |
vastuto 'karttā muktavat sākṣivadudāsīnaḥ |
sattvarajastamāṃsi kartḥṇi karmāṇyapi bhavanti |
akarttā 'pi puruṣaḥ kartteva vyavahriyate |
acoraścoraiḥ saha dhṛtaścora eva |
guṇābhedāt prakṛtiḥ kartrī na puruṣaḥ |
darśanaśaktimataḥ kriyāśaktirahitasya puruṣasya pradhānena saha saṃyogaḥ mahadādibhūtaparyantaṃ pradhānaṃ draṣṭum |
darśanaśaktirahitasya kriyāśaktimataḥ pradhānasyāpi puruṣeṇa saṃyogaḥ mokṣārthaṃ puruṣasya bhinnatvena vyaktāvyaktapuruṣajñāne jāte pradhānasya mokṣo bhavati |
nityasukhopalabdhirmokṣa iti cedupalabdherapi nityānityavivekagrastatvādasāram |
na ca nityasukhagocarasyāvidyādiyatkiñcidāvaraṇabhaṅga eva puruṣārtho vācyaḥ sukhānubhavasyaiva puruṣārthatvāccaitanyanityatvenāvaraṇasyāpi asambhavācca |
mokṣe paramānandaśrutismṛtayastu mokṣaśāstraparibhāṣāmātrā |
body.translated_text: For this very reason, the real transformation that is otherwise-becoming is characterized precisely by the definition of <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation); and <s>pariṇāma</s> is accepted. And that <s>Puruṣa</s> is distinct for each body — in this and other [matters], because of non-modification. In reality, [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is a non-agent, like one who is liberated, a witness, and indifferent. <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are the agents and also become the actions. Though <s>Puruṣa</s> is a non-agent, he is spoken of as if an agent — just as a non-thief, when seized together with thieves, is treated as a thief. Due to non-difference from the <s>guṇas</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s> is the agent, not <s>Puruṣa</s>. The conjunction of <s>Puruṣa</s>, who possesses the power of seeing but lacks the power of action, with <s>Pradhāna</s>, is for the purpose of seeing <s>Pradhāna</s> [in its modifications] up to the gross elements beginning with <s>Mahat</s>. The conjunction of <s>Pradhāna</s>, which lacks the power of seeing but possesses the power of action, with <s>Puruṣa</s>, is for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation; when the knowledge of the distinctness of the manifest, the unmanifest, and <s>Puruṣa</s> arises, liberation of <s>Pradhāna</s> occurs. If it be said that liberation is the attainment of eternal bliss — [we reply that] since even such attainment is subject to the discrimination of the eternal and non-eternal, this is without substance. Nor should the removal of whatever obstruction of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and so forth, pertaining to the object of eternal bliss, be called the goal of <s>Puruṣa</s> — because the experience of bliss itself is the goal of <s>Puruṣa</s>, and because, consciousness being eternal, such an obstruction is itself impossible. The <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> passages speaking of supreme bliss in liberation are merely technical terminology of the liberation-teachings.

children.translated_text: There is only suffering, not pleasure, since that [suffering] alone is experienced;
when one afflicted by suffering finds a remedy, the designation 'pleasure' is applied.

body.translated_text: Suffering is the expectation of sensual pleasure; pleasure is remembered as the cessation of suffering.

body.text:
ityādismṛtibhirduḥkhanivṛttireva sukhatvena paribhāṣitā |
sāṃkhyasūtramapi duḥkhanivṛttirgauṇa iti vimuktipraśaṃsā mandānāmiti ca |
ānandāvāptistu gauṇamokṣo brahmaloke bhavati iti paścāt kṛtārthayoḥ pradhānapuruṣayorviyogo bhavati andhapaṅgusaṃyogavat |
tathāhi ekaḥ paṅguraparaścāndhaḥ dvāvapyetau duṣṭe pathi gacchantau mahatā sārthena saha daivādbandhubhiḥ parityaktau yathāyogaṃ gamanaśaktidarśanaśaktirahitau darśanārthaṃ gamanārthaṃ ca saṃyuktau bhavataḥ |
tathā cāndhena paṅguḥ skandhamāropitastaddarśitamārgeṇāndho yāti paṅguścāndhaskandhārūḍhaḥ san yāti |
paścāt svasvadeśaprāptyanantaraṃ kṛtārthau santau viyuktau bhavataḥ |
tathā ca pradhānaṃ puruṣasya mokṣaṃ kṛtvā nivarttate |
puruṣo na pravarttate nāpi nivarttate |
draṣṭā bhoktā ca puruṣaḥ |
bhogaścidavasānatā lakṣaṇaḥ |
na kriyāveśātmā sa ca puruṣaḥ anādyavivekāt saṃsarati |
sacchāstraśravaṇena gurvanugraheṇa ca nirvicikitso vivekajñāne jāte mucyate |
prakṛtipuruṣasaṃyogāt saṃsāraḥ sañjāyate |
strīpuruṣasaṃyogādapatyamiva prakṛtermahattatvaṃ jāyate |
mahattatvādahaṅkāro jāyate |
sa ca trividhaḥ vaikāriko bhūtādistaijasaśca |
yo hi vaikarikaḥ sa eva sāttvikaḥ yo bhūtādiḥ sa eva tāmasaḥ |
yo hi taijasaḥ sa eva rājasaḥ tatra vaikārikādahaṅkārādekādaśendriyāṇi tadabhimāninyo devatāśca jāyante |
bhūtādeścāhaṃkārāt tanmātrāṇi jāyante taijasādahaṃkārādekādaśendriyagaṇastanmātrapañcakaṃ ca jāyate |
etadgaṇadvayasya yathāsaṃkhyaṃ vaikārikādbhūtādeścāhaṃkārājjātatvāt kathaṃ punarutpattirucyata iti cecchṛṇu |
body.translated_text: By such <s>smṛti</s> statements, the cessation of suffering alone is defined as happiness. The <s>Sāṃkhya Sūtra</s> also [states]: 'The cessation of suffering is secondary' — thus the praise of liberation is mild. But the attainment of bliss is secondary liberation occurring in <s>Brahmaloka</s>. Thereafter, when both have fulfilled their purpose, the separation of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> occurs, like the conjunction of the blind and the lame. For indeed, one is lame and another is blind — these two, traveling on a difficult path, abandoned by their kinsmen by fate while journeying with a great caravan, lacking respectively the power of locomotion and the power of sight, become united for the purpose of seeing and going. Thus the lame man, mounted on the shoulder of the blind man, directs the path, and the blind man walks; and the lame man, mounted on the blind man's shoulder, also travels. Afterwards, upon arriving at their respective destinations, having fulfilled their purpose, they separate. Likewise, <s>Pradhāna</s>, having accomplished the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>, ceases activity. <s>Puruṣa</s> neither acts nor ceases to act. <s>Puruṣa</s> is the seer and the experiencer. And experience has the nature of termination of consciousness. That <s>Puruṣa</s> is not of the nature of involvement in action — due to beginningless non-discrimination, he transmigrates. Through hearing the true scriptures and by the grace of the teacher, when doubt-free discriminative knowledge arises, he is liberated. From the conjunction of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) arises. Just as offspring arise from the union of woman and man, from <s>Prakṛti</s> arises <s>Mahat-tattva</s> (the Great Principle). From <s>Mahat-tattva</s> arises <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (the I-principle). And that is threefold: <s>vaikārika</s> (modified), <s>bhūtādi</s> (elemental), and <s>taijasa</s> (luminous). That which is <s>vaikārika</s> is indeed <s>sāttvika</s>; that which is <s>bhūtādi</s> is indeed <s>tāmasa</s>. That which is <s>taijasa</s> is indeed <s>rājasa</s>. From the <s>vaikārika ahaṃkāra</s>, the eleven organs and the deities presiding over them arise. From the <s>bhūtādi ahaṃkāra</s>, the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) arise. From the <s>taijasa ahaṃkāra</s>, the group of eleven organs and the fivefold <s>tanmātras</s> arise. Since these two groups arise respectively from the <s>vaikārika</s> and <s>bhūtādi ahaṃkāra</s>, how then is their origin from the <s>taijasa</s> stated? Listen:

children.text: yadā rajastamasī abhibhūya sattvaguṇa utkaṭo vaikarikasañjñāṃ labhamāno 'haṃkāro 'pravṛttidharmā taijasāhaṃkāraṃ sahāyīkṛtya pravṛttidharmāṇyekādaśendriyāṇi janayati tadā tāni svasāhāyyacchalamadhigamya taijasasvarūpeṇāpi kṛtānītyucyate |
children.translated_text: When <s>sattva-guṇa</s>, suppressing <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, becomes predominant, the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> gaining the designation <s>vaikārika</s>, being itself of the nature of non-activity, taking the <s>taijasa ahaṃkāra</s> as its auxiliary, generates the eleven organs which are of the nature of activity. Then those [organs], having attained [their existence] under the pretext of its [the <s>taijasa</s>'s] assistance, are said to have been produced by the <s>taijasa</s> nature as well.
