children.text: yadā ca sattvarajasī abhibhūya tamoguṇotkaṭo bhūtādistaijasāhaṃkārasya rūpaṃ sahāyīkṛtya tanmātrapañcakaṃ pravṛttidharmakaṃ karoti tadā tattanmātrapañcakaṃ svasāhāyyenaiva taijasenāpi kṛtamityucyate tasmāt pravṛttidharmakāt tattanmātrapañcakād bhūtapañcakamutpadyate |
children.translated_text: And when <s>tamo-guṇa</s>, suppressing <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>, becomes predominant, the <s>bhūtādi</s>, taking the form of the <s>taijasa ahaṃkāra</s> as its auxiliary, makes the fivefold <s>tanmātras</s> of the nature of activity. Then that fivefold group of <s>tanmātras</s> is said to have been produced by the <s>taijasa</s> as well, through its own assistance. From those fivefold <s>tanmātras</s>, which are of the nature of activity, the five gross elements arise.
This is the sequence of transformation.
From the <s>vaikārika</s> come the eleven organs; from the <s>bhūtādi</s> come the five <s>tanmātras</s>.

body.text:
ayamarthaḥ |
vaikārikasya bhūtādeśca svasvapravṛttidharmakakāryadvayasya yathāsaṃkhyaṃ janane taijasāhaṃkārasya sāhāyyam |
taijasāhaṃkārasya sāhāyyakaraṇādeva etadgaṇadvayalakṣaṇakakāryasya pravṛttidharmakatvam |
buddhijanakānīndriyāṇi buddhīndriyāṇi tāni cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇarasanatvagindriyāṇi |
teṣāṃ ca viṣayāḥ rūpaśabdagandharasasparśāḥ |
karma kurvantīti karmendriyāṇi tāni ca vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāni |
teṣāṃ ca viṣayāḥ vāgvadanādānagamanotsargānandāḥ |
mano buddhīndriyaṃ karmendriyaṃ ca yato buddhīndriyāṇāṃ vṛttiṃ saṃkalpayati karmendriyāṇāṃ ca ata ubhayātmakaṃ manaḥ |
mano 'pi vibhu dharmādharmavāsanāśrayataḥ pratipuruṣamantaḥkaraṇaṃ nityamākāśavat |
na ca prakṛtidharmā eva santvadṛṣṭādaya iti vācyam anyaniṣṭhādṛṣṭādibhiranyatra sukhaduḥkhādyutpāde 'tiprasaṅgāt |
tacca nāṇu saṃbhavati yogināṃ sarvāvacchedena ekadā 'khilasākṣātkārāsambhavāt |
na ca yogināṃ yogajadharma eva pratyāsattiḥ syāt saṃyogasaṃyuktasamavāyādilaukikapratyāsattyaivopapattau sannikarṣāntarakalpane mānābhāvāt gauravācca anyonyavyabhicārācca |
sākṣātkāreṣvavāntarajātikalpane jātisāṅkaryāt atigauravācca |
yogimate sarvārthagrahaṇasamarthasyāntaḥkaraṇasya tamaākhyāvaraṇabhaṅga eva yogajadharmādibhiḥ kriyate suṣuptau tamaso vṛttipratibandhakatvasiddheriti nāpyantaḥkaraṇaṃ madhyamaparimāṇamātraṃ sambhavati pralaye vināśenādṛṣṭādyādhāratānupapatteḥ ataḥ pariśeṣato 'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ vibhveva sidyati taduktam |
body.translated_text: The meaning is this: in the respective generation of the two products belonging to the <s>vaikārika</s> and <s>bhūtādi</s>, which are of the nature of activity, the <s>taijasa ahaṃkāra</s> serves as the auxiliary. It is precisely because the <s>taijasa ahaṃkāra</s> renders this assistance that the product characterized as these two groups possesses the nature of activity. The organs that generate cognitions are the <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (organs of knowledge) — they are the organs of sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. Their objects are form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. Those that perform action are the <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action) — they are speech, hands, feet, the organ of excretion, and the organ of generation. Their functions are speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure. <s>Manas</s> (mind) is both a <s>buddhīndriya</s> and a <s>karmendriya</s>, because it deliberates upon the functioning of the knowledge organs and also of the action organs — therefore <s>manas</s> is of a twofold nature. <s>Manas</s> is also all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>), being the locus of <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) for each individual <s>puruṣa</s> — the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner organ) is eternal like space. Nor can it be said that <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit/demerit) and the like are properties of <s>Prakṛti</s> alone, for then the absurd consequence would follow that one person's <s>adṛṣṭa</s> would produce pleasure and pain in another. And it cannot be atomic in size, for <s>yogins</s> would then be unable to perceive everything at once in all its delimitations. Nor should <s>yogins</s>' perception be explained by a special <s>yoga</s>-born <s>dharma</s> as the connecting link, since the ordinary connecting links of conjunction, inherence in what is conjoined, and the like suffice — there being no evidence for positing a special connection, and because of the undue complexity, and because of mutual deviation. Positing a special sub-class among perceptions would lead to confusion of categories and excessive complexity. In the <s>Yoga</s> system, the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>, which is capable of grasping all objects, merely has its obscuration called <s>tamas</s> broken by <s>yoga</s>-born <s>dharma</s> and the like — since the capacity of <s>tamas</s> to obstruct mental functioning is established in deep sleep. Therefore the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> cannot be of merely medium size; in dissolution, its destruction would leave no substratum for <s>adṛṣṭa</s> and the like. Hence, by elimination, the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> is established as all-pervading. Thus it is said:

children.translated_text: 'The space of mind (<s>cittākāśa</s>), the space of consciousness (<s>cidākāśa</s>), and space (<s>ākāśa</s>) as the third —
Know that <s>cidākāśa</s> (the space of consciousness) is the most empty of the two, O fair-faced one.'
An objection may arise:

Even if the all-pervading nature of the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> explains the attainment of delimited mental functions through obscuration, transmigration to other worlds and the like would not be possible.

children.text: ata eva sāṃkhyasūtram "na vyāpakaṃ manaḥ karaṇatvā"diti |
children.translated_text: Hence the <s>Sāṃkhya Sūtra</s> states: '<s>Manas</s> is not all-pervading, because it is an instrument.'

children.text: tadgatiśruteriti veti kiṃ caivaṃ sati lāghavāt caitanyasyaivāvaraṇakalpanamucitaṃ kimarthaṃ vibhvantaḥkaraṇaṃ parikalpyate tatra jñānapratibandhakamāvaraṇaṃ kalpyate ||
children.translated_text: 'Because of the <s>śruti</s> about its movement' — what then? Moreover, if this is so, then by the principle of parsimony, it would be appropriate to posit obscuration of consciousness itself — why should an all-pervading <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> be posited? And therein, an obscuration that obstructs knowledge would need to be posited.

body.text:
atrocyate |
gatiśrutistāvat ātmanīvāntaḥkaraṇe 'pi prāṇendriyādyupādhinopapadyate kāryakāraṇarūpeṇāntaḥkaraṇadvaitāt |
kāryāntaḥkaraṇasya svato 'pi gatirupapadyate kāryakāraṇarūpeṇāntaḥkaraṇadvaitaṃ ca sāṃkhyairapyeṣṭavyam kevalakāryatve 'ntaḥkaraṇadharmatvaṃ dharmādīnāmiti sāṃkhyasūtrānupapatteḥ |
kevalanityatve ca mahadādyutpattisūtrānupapatteḥ yattūktaṃ caitanyasyaivāvaraṇakalpanaṃ yuktamiti tadayuktam |
kūṭasthacaitanyasya jñānapratibandharūpāvaraṇāsambhavāt |
na ca caitanyasyārthasambandha eva pratibimbādirūpe pratibandhakaṃ kalpanīyamiti vācyam evamapyātmadarśanānupapatteḥ karaṇadvāraṃ vinā svasmin pratibimbādirūpeṇa svasvasambandhāsambhavāt |
api ca icchākṛtyādyādhāratayā 'ntaḥkaraṇe siddhe svapnādāvantardṛśyamānaghaṭādayo 'pi tasyaiva pariṇāmāḥ kalpyante kāryakāraṇayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaucityāt |
evaṃ ca ghaṭādyākārapariṇatāścaitanye bhāsante tadavibhāgenaiva bāhyaghaṭādikaṃ bhāsate 'tastādṛśapariṇāmapratibandhakamevāvaraṇaṃ tatraiva yuktaṃ kiñca bāhyakaraṇasyāvaraṇadarśanenāntarāvaraṇasyāpi karaṇaniṣṭhatvaṃ cānumīyate ātmano 'nāvṛtatvaṃ śrutismṛtibhyāṃ ceti |
body.translated_text: To this we reply: the <s>śruti</s> about movement is explained by the limiting adjuncts of <s>prāṇa</s>, organs, and the like — for the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> as well, just as for the <s>ātman</s> — due to the duality of the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> in the forms of cause and effect. The movement of the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> in its effect-form is possible even on its own account. And the duality of the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> as cause and effect must be accepted even by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, for if the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> were purely an effect, the <s>Sāṃkhya Sūtra</s> stating that <s>dharma</s> and the like are properties of the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> would be untenable. And if it were purely eternal, the sūtras about the production of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest would be untenable. As for the objection that it is appropriate to posit obscuration of consciousness itself — that is incorrect. For the changeless consciousness cannot have obscuration in the form of obstruction of knowledge. Nor can it be said that in the relationship of consciousness with objects, an obstruction in the form of reflection and the like should be posited — for even so, self-knowledge would be inexplicable, since without the medium of an instrument, a relationship of self with self in the form of reflection and the like would be impossible. Moreover, since the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> is established as the substratum of desire, will, and the like, the pots and other objects seen internally in dreams are also to be regarded as its transformations — due to the propriety of co-reference between cause and effect. And thus, the transformations in the form of pots and the like shine in consciousness, and through non-distinction from that, external pots and the like also shine. Therefore, obscuration as an obstruction to such transformation is properly located in the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> alone. Furthermore, from the observation that external organs have obscuration, the obscuration of the internal [organ] too is inferred to belong to the instrument. And the unobscured nature of the <s>ātman</s> is established by both <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.

body.text: nanvantaḥkaraṇasya vibhutve sati kathaṃ kāryatvaṃ syāditi cenna vibhvyā api ākaśaprakṛteḥ kāryākāśarūpaparicchinnapariṇāmavad guṇāntarasambhedenāntaḥkaraṇaprakṛterapi paricchinnāntaḥkaraṇarūpapariṇāmopapattiḥ śrutismṛtiprāmāṇyāccaitadiṣyata iti dik ||
body.translated_text: If it be objected: how can the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> be an effect if it is all-pervading? — this is not a valid objection. For just as space, though all-pervading as a cause (<s>ākāśa-prakṛti</s>), undergoes delimited transformation in the form of effect-space (<s>kāryākāśa</s>), so too, through the distinction of other <s>guṇas</s>, delimited transformation in the form of the [effect-]<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> from the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>-as-cause is possible. This is accepted on the authority of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> — this is the general direction [of the argument].

body.text:
manasaḥ saṅkalpo viṣayaḥ |
etānyekādaśa vaikṛtāhaṃkārājjātāni ityavādi smaiva buddhipratibimbitamarthaṃ puruṣa upalabhate |

children.translated_text: Thus it is said: <s>Puruṣa</s> cognizes the object situated in <s>buddhi</s>.
'I shall perform <s>dharma</s>' — such determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is the defining characteristic of <s>buddhi</s>.
<s>Dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereignty — these belong to <s>sāttvika buddhi</s>.
The opposite — non-dispassion and the like — is <s>tāmasa</s>.

body.translated_text: The object of <s>manas</s> is <s>saṅkalpa</s> (deliberation/intention). These eleven [organs] arise from the <s>vaikṛta ahaṃkāra</s> — this has already been stated. <s>Puruṣa</s> apprehends the object reflected in <s>buddhi</s>.

children.text: pañcaviṃśatitattvaireva jagadvyāptaṃ na nyūnairnādhikaiśca vatsavivṛddhinimittaṃ kṣīrasyeva ajñasyāpi pradhānasya puruṣamokṣārthaṃ pravṛttirucitaiva |
children.translated_text: The world is pervaded by the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> alone — neither fewer nor more. Just as milk [flows] for the growth of a calf, so too the activity of unintelligent <s>Pradhāna</s> for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation is entirely appropriate.

children.text: liṅgaśarīraṃ tu buddhyahaṃkāramanobuddhīndriyakarmendriyapañcatanmātrāṇāmaṣṭādaśānāṃ samudāyaḥ trayoviṃśatitattvamadhye pañcabhūtāni varjayitvā ahaṃkāraṃ ca buddhau praveśya saptadaśakaṃ liṅgaśarīrasañjñaṃ bhavati vahnerindhanavadātmano 'bhivyaktisthānavāt |
children.translated_text: The subtle body (<s>liṅga-śarīra</s>) is the aggregate of eighteen [principles]: <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, the five <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (organs of knowledge), the five <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). Among the twenty-three <s>tattvas</s>, excluding the five gross elements and subsuming <s>ahaṃkāra</s> within <s>buddhi</s>, the group of seventeen is designated the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s> (subtle body), because it serves as the locus of the self's manifestation, just as fuel [is the locus of manifestation] for fire.

children.text: tacca sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ sargādāvutpadya prākṛtapralayaparyantaṃ tiṣṭhati tena caiveha lokaparalokayoḥ saṃsaraṇaṃ jīvānāṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: And that [subtle body], arising for all puruṣas at the beginning of creation, persists until prākṛta-pralaya (dissolution into Prakṛti). Through it alone, the transmigration of living beings occurs in this world and the next.

children.text: prāṇaśca buddhereva vṛttibheda ityato na liṅgaśarīrāt pṛthaṅ nirdiśyate tasya ca liṅgaśarīrasya sūkṣmāṇi pañca bhūtāni āśrayaścitrādivadāśrayaṃ vinā paramasūkṣmasya lokāntaragamanāsambhavāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is but a modification of <s>buddhi</s>, and therefore it is not enumerated separately from the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s> (subtle body). And for that subtle body, the five subtle elements serve as its support — for without a support, like a painting without a canvas, the movement of the supremely subtle [body] to another world would be impossible.

body.text:
idaṃ ca liṅgaśarīramādau svayaṃbhuva upādhibhūtamekameva jāyate tasyaiva virāḍākhyavakṣyamāṇasthūlaśarīravat tataśca vyaṣṭijīvānāmupādhibhūtāni vyaṣṭiliṅgaśarīrāṇi tadaṃśabhūtāni tato vibhajyante |
piturliṅgaśarīrāt puttraliṅgaśarīravat |
taduktaṃ sūtrakāreṇa |
vyaktibhedaḥ karmaviśeṣāditi manunāpyuktam |
body.translated_text: And this <s>liṅga-śarīra</s>, in the beginning, is born as one single [body], serving as the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of the Self-born (<s>Svayambhu</s>), just like his gross body called <s>Virāṭ</s> which will be described. And from that, the individual <s>liṅga-śarīras</s>, which are portions thereof, serving as the limiting adjuncts of individual souls (<s>vyaṣṭi-jīvas</s>), are divided out — like the son's subtle body from the father's subtle body. Thus it has been stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras). The distinction of individuals arises from the distinction of <s>karma</s> — thus <s>Manu</s> has also said.

body.text:
teṣāṃ tvavayavān sūkṣmān ṣaṇṇāmapyamitaujasām /
  sanniveśyātmamātrāsu sarvabhūtāni nirmame // iti /
body.translated_text: 'Combining the subtle parts of those six of immeasurable power, into his own self-portions, he created all beings.'

body.text:
ṣaṇṇāmiti ṣaḍindriyaṃ samastaliṅgaśarīropalakṣakam tathā ca svayambhūḥ svaliṅgaśarīrāvayavān sūkṣmānalpān ātmamātrāsu svāṃśacetaneṣu saṃyojya sarvaprāṇinaḥ sasarjjetyartha iti liṅgaśarīram |
sthūlaśarīrotpattistu daśaguṇitamahattattvamadhye 'haṃkārastasyāpi daśaguṇitasya madhye vyomno 'pi daśaguṇitasya madhye vāyurvāyorapi daśaguṇitasya madhye tejastejaso 'pi daśaguṇitasya madhye jalaṃ jalasyāpi daśaguṇitasya madhye pṛthivī samutpadyate saiva ca sthūlaśarīrasya bījaṃ tadeva ca pṛthivīrūpaṃ bījamaṇḍarūpeṇa pariṇamate tasyāpi daśaguṇitāṇḍarūpasya pṛthivyāvaraṇasya madhye caturdaśabhuvanātmakaṃ svayambhuvaḥ sthūlaśarīraṃ tatsaṃkalpādevotpadyate tenaiva śarīreṇa svayambhūrnārāyaṇa ityucyate |
taduktaṃ manunā svayambhuvaṃ prakṛtya |
body.translated_text: 'Of the six' — the six organs are representative of the entire <s>liṅga-śarīra</s>. And thus <s>Svayambhu</s>, combining the subtle, small portions of his own <s>liṅga-śarīra</s> into the <s>ātma-mātrās</s> — that is, into the conscious beings who are his own fragments — created all creatures. This is the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s>. The origin of the gross body (<s>sthūla-śarīra</s>), however, [is as follows]: within the tenfold-magnified <s>Mahat-tattva</s> is <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>; within its tenfold magnification is space (<s>vyoman</s>); within the tenfold magnification of space is air (<s>vāyu</s>); within the tenfold magnification of air is fire (<s>tejas</s>); within the tenfold magnification of fire is water (<s>jala</s>); within the tenfold magnification of water, earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) arises. That earth itself is the seed of the gross body. That very seed in the form of earth transforms into the form of the cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>). Within that tenfold-magnified egg, which is the envelope of earth, the gross body of <s>Svayambhu</s> consisting of the fourteen worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>) arises by his very intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>). Through that body, <s>Svayambhu</s> is called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Thus <s>Manu</s> has said, referring to <s>Svayambhu</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Desiring to create diverse beings from his own body,
He first created the waters, and deposited his seed in them.
That [seed] became a golden egg, radiant as the sun with a thousand rays.
In that [egg], <s>Brahmā</s> himself [was born] — the grandfather of all the worlds.

children.text: sa vai śarīrī prathamaḥ sa vai puruṣa ucyate /
children.translated_text: He indeed was the first embodied being; he indeed is called <s>Puruṣa</s>.
He, the original creator of beings, <s>Brahmā</s>, came into being first.

body.text:
āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ /
  tā yadasyāyanaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // ityādineti /
body.translated_text: The waters are called <s>nārāḥ</s>, for the waters are indeed the offspring of <s>Nara</s>. Since they were his first abode (<s>ayana</s>), he is therefore called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.' And so forth.

body.text:
tata eva cādipuruṣāt vyaṣṭipuruṣāṇāṃ vibhāgādante ca tatraiva layāt sa eva caika ātmeti śrutismṛtyorvyavahriyate ato na vyavahāraparatayā nārāyaṇa eva sarvabhūtānāmātmetyādiśrutismṛtivirodha iti |
tataśca sa nārāyaṇo virāṭśarīrī svanābhikamalakarṇikāsthānīyasya sumerorupari caturmukhākhyaṃ svayaṃbhuvaṃ sṛṣṭvā taddvārānyānapi vyaṣṭiśarīriṇaḥ sthāvarāntān sasarja taduktam -
body.translated_text: And therefore, since individual <s>puruṣas</s> are divided out from that primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, and at the end dissolve back into him, he alone is referred to as the one <s>Ātman</s> in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. Therefore there is no contradiction with <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> statements of the conventional kind such as '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is the <s>Ātman</s> of all beings.' And then that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, embodied in the <s>Virāṭ</s> body, having created <s>Svayambhu</s> called <s>Caturmukha</s> (four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>) upon <s>Sumeru</s> — which occupies the position of the pericarp of his own navel-lotus — through him created other individual embodied beings down to immovable things. Thus it is said:

body.text:
taccharīrasamutpannaiḥ kāryaistaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ saha /
  kṣetrajñāḥ samajāyanta gātrebhyastasya dhīmataḥ // iti /
body.translated_text: 'From his body were born the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (knowers of the field), along with those effects and causes that arose from the body of that wise one.'

children.text: yattu śeṣaśāyino nārāyaṇasya nābhikamalaśrotracakṣurādibhyaścaturmukhasyāvirbhāvaḥ śrūyate taddainyandinasargeṣveva kalpabhedena mantavyam |
children.translated_text: As for the <s>śruti</s> account that <s>Caturmukha</s> (four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>) manifests from the navel-lotus, ears, eyes, and other parts of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> reclining on <s>Śeṣa</s> — that should be understood as referring only to the daily creation cycles, varying by <s>kalpa</s>.

children.text: dainandinapralayeṣveva hi nārāyaṇaśarīre praviśyaikībhūya suptānāṃ devānāṃ caturmukhādikrameṇāvirbhāvaḥ śeṣaśāyinaḥ sakāśāt ghaṭate na tvādisargeṣu dainandinapralaya eva līlāvigraheṇa śayanāditi ||
children.translated_text: For it is only in the daily dissolutions that the gods, having entered the body of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and become merged in sleep, manifest again through <s>Caturmukha</s> and the subsequent sequence from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> reclining on <s>Śeṣa</s> — this is coherent. But in the original creation, the daily dissolution alone [involves] reclining with a sport-form (<s>līlā-vigraha</s>).

body.text:
tadevaṃ saṃkṣepataścaturviṃśatitattvāni teṣāṃ sṛṣṭikṣayaṃ prayojanaṃ coktam |
tatra yadyasmājjāyate tasya tadā '; 'pūraṇenaiva sthitiḥ tatastasya saṃhāro 'pi tatraiva bhavati |
tathā ca bhārate |
body.translated_text: Thus, the twenty-four <s>tattvas</s>, their creation, dissolution, and purpose have been stated in brief. Therein, whatever arises from whatever — its continuance is through the 'filling up' by that very [source]; and its dissolution also occurs back into that very [source]. And thus in the <s>Bhārata</s>:

body.text:
yadyasmājjāyate tattvaṃ tacca tatra pralīyate /
  līyante pratilomāni jāyante cottarottaram // iti /
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>tattva</s> arises from whatever, it dissolves back into that. They dissolve in reverse order and arise in forward succession.'

body.text: ete ca sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārarūpāḥ sthūlā eva pariṇāmāścaturviṃśatitattvānāṃ kūṭasthapuruṣavivekāya pradarśitāḥ sūkṣmā apyanye pratikṣaṇapariṇāmā eteṣāṃ smaryante |
body.translated_text: These gross transformations of the twenty-four <s>tattvas</s> — in the forms of creation, sustenance, and dissolution — have been demonstrated for the purpose of discriminating the changeless (<s>kūṭastha</s>) <s>Puruṣa</s>. Other subtle, moment-by-moment transformations of these [<s>tattvas</s>] are also mentioned:

body.text:
nityadāhyaṅgabhūtāni bhavanti na bhavanti ca /
  kālenālakṣyavegena sūkṣmatvāt tanna gṛhyate // iti /
body.translated_text: 'The parts that constitute the eternally consumed are arising and ceasing at every moment. Due to the subtlety of the imperceptibly swift passage of time, this is not perceived.'

body.text:
atastu sarvaṃ jaḍavastu paramārthataḥ sarvadaivāsaducyate |
tataśca tasmādvirajya ātmaiva paramārthasatyo duḥkhabhīrubhirdraṣṭavyaḥ taduktam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, all insentient substance is, in ultimate reality, at all times unreal (<s>asat</s>). Hence, turning away from that, the <s>Ātman</s> alone — which is ultimately real — should be realized by those who fear suffering. Thus it is said:

children.translated_text: The great [tree], whose seed is the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>), whose trunk is <s>Buddhi</s>,
Whose knots are <s>Mahā-ahaṃkāra</s> (the great I-principle), whose cavities are the sprouts of the organs,
Whose great branches are the gross elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>), whose secondary branches are the <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars),
Ever bearing leaves, ever bearing flowers, yielding fruits of good and evil,
Is the eternal tree of <s>Brahman</s>, the sustenance of all beings.
Knowing this in truth, with the supreme sword of knowledge,

body.text: kṛtvā cākṣaratāṃ prāpya jahāti mṛtyujanmanī // iti /
body.translated_text: Having cut [this tree] and attained the state of the imperishable, one abandons death and birth.

children.translated_text: Thus it is said:
'The organs and the objects of the organs do not approach [that state]; therefore indeed,
The embodied one, devoid of instruments, does not merit a body again.'

body.translated_text: 'Therefore, from attachment belonging to the all-pervading Self, all creatures are born.'

body.text: narakādau viśeṣarāgābhāve 'pi sāmānyarāgasattvādrāgasya karmasahakāritvaṃ viṣākārambhe tadeva saktaḥ saha karmaṇaiti liṅgaṃ mano yatra niṣaktamasyeti śrutāvabhimānarāgadveṣādijanyasya viṣyavāsanākhyasaṅgasāmānyasyaiva janmādiviṣākārambhe sahakāritvasiddheḥ |
body.translated_text: Even in the absence of specific attachment to hellish realms and the like, mere general attachment (<s>sāmānya-rāga</s>) suffices — attachment cooperates with <s>karma</s> in initiating the particular realm of experience. 'Attached, he goes together with his <s>karma</s>'; 'the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) and <s>manas</s> are attached to wherever they are fixed' — from these <s>śruti</s> passages, the cooperation of the general attachment called object-<s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions of objects) — born of prideful attachment, aversion, and the like — in initiating the particular realm of experience through birth and the like is established.

body.text:
yatra yatra mano dehī dhārayet sakalaṃ dhiyā /
  snehād dveṣād guṇādvāpi yāti tattatsarūpatām // iti smṛteḥ /

children.translated_text: 'He, having withdrawn his senses, instructed by the mirror of the teacher,
Straightaway perceived the modifications, arising from delusion, as other than himself.'

body.translated_text: 'Wherever the embodied one steadily fixes the mind with full intellect, whether through affection, aversion, or [natural] quality — he attains that very form.' — Thus says the <s>smṛti</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Then [he realized]: this <s>Prakṛti</s> is not I, for she is of an impure nature.
I am of a pure and enlightened nature — knowing this, he renounces her.'
'Thus, when the self is recognized as pure, distinct from body, organs, and the rest,

children.text: nikhilā savikāreyaṃ tyak taprāyā hi carmavat //
children.translated_text: This entire [<s>Prakṛti</s>] with all her modifications is virtually cast off, like a [shed] skin.'

body.text: nanvanātmanyātmabuddhirūpā yā 'vidyā tasyāḥ kathamātmaviśeṣyakavivekajñānanāśyatvaṃ prakārādibhedāditi cet na tādṛśāvidyāyā anātmaviśeṣyakavivekadvāreṇātmaviśeṣyakavivekanāśyatvāditi |

children.translated_text: And the non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> that arises through <s>Yoga</s> —

children.text: tadvivekajñānadvāraiva mokṣakāraṇaṃ bhavati na tu sākṣāt |
children.translated_text: That leads to liberation only through the medium of discriminative knowledge (<s>viveka-jñāna</s>), not directly.

children.text: avidyānivartakatvābhāvāt ahaṃ gauraḥ karttā sukhī duḥkhītyādijñānameva hyavidyā saṃsārānarthahetutayā śrutismṛtinyāyasiddhā tasyāśca nivarttikā nāhaṃ gaura ityādirūpā vivekakhyātireva bhavati samāne viṣaye grāhyābhāvatvaprakārakagrāhyābhāvajñānatvenaiva virodhāt anyathā muktinirvikalpakasyāpi idaṃ rajatamiti jñānavirodhitvāpatteḥ |
children.translated_text: Because it does not [directly] remove <s>avidyā</s>. For <s>avidyā</s> — established by <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and reasoning as the cause of the miseries of <s>saṃsāra</s> — consists in cognitions such as 'I am fair,' 'I am the agent,' 'I am happy,' 'I am suffering,' and the like. And the remover of that is only <s>viveka-khyāti</s> (discriminative discernment) in the form 'I am not fair' and the like, since the opposition consists precisely in the fact that within the same domain, one cognition grasps the absence of what the other grasps. Otherwise, even the non-conceptual cognition [arising from <s>Yoga</s>] would absurdly conflict with the cognition 'this is silver' [in a case of error]. Moreover, since the capacity to oppose the erroneous cognition necessarily belongs to the said absence-cognition, the capacity of non-conceptual knowledge to remove error need not be separately postulated — that would be needlessly complex.

children.text: kiñca yathoktābhāvajñāne grāhyajñānavirodhitvasyāvaśyakatayā nirvikalpajñānasya bhramanivartakatvaṃ na pṛthak kalpyate gauravāt ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, since the capacity to oppose the erroneous cognition necessarily belongs to the said absence-cognition, the capacity of non-conceptual knowledge to remove error need not be separately postulated — that would be needlessly complex.

body.translated_text: If it be objected: ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), which is the superimposition of the self upon the non-self, how can it be destroyed by discriminative knowledge (<s>viveka-jñāna</s>) that has the self as its qualificand, given the difference in qualificand and other aspects? This is not a valid objection — because such <s>avidyā</s> is destroyed by discriminative knowledge with the self as qualificand through the medium of discrimination with the non-self as qualificand.

body.text: api ca athāta ādeśo neti neti na hyetasmāditi netyanyat paramastītyādiśrutyā vivekopadeśāpekṣayottama upadeśo nāstītyucyate ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>śruti</s> itself, with the passage 'Now the instruction: neti neti (not this, not this) — for there is nothing higher than this, that it is not' and the like, declares that there is no instruction superior to discriminative instruction (<s>viveka-upadeśa</s>).

children.translated_text: 'But those who, with the eye of knowledge, perceive the difference between the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) and the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>),

children.text: bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye viduryānti te param //
children.translated_text: And [perceive] the liberation of beings from <s>Prakṛti</s> — they attain the Supreme.'

body.text: iti gītāvākyaiśca vivekajñānasyaiva mokṣahetutvamucyate 'to vivekajñānameva sākṣādavidyānivṛttyā mokṣahetuḥ |

children.translated_text: The direct realization of the <s>Ātman</s> alone through <s>Yoga</s>, however, through the method of qualified non-apprehension (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>), reveals the absence of properties belonging to limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) and the like, and also the distinctness from the limiting adjuncts. From that follows the removal of <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: etena sarvabhūteṣu samatājñānam ātmanaḥ sarvātmakatvādijñānaṃ ca śrutismṛtyorgīyamānaṃ vivekajñānasyaiva śeṣabhūtaṃ sarvadarśaneṣu mantavyam |
children.translated_text: By this, the knowledge of equality of the self in all beings, the knowledge of the self's all-pervasive nature, and the like — celebrated in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> — should be understood in all philosophical systems as subordinate to <s>viveka-jñāna</s> (discriminative knowledge).

children.text: jñānāntarāṇāṃ sākṣādabhimānānivartakatvāt brahmamīmāṃsāyāṃ tvayaṃ viśeṣo yatparamātmavivekaśeṣatvam |
children.translated_text: Other types of knowledge cannot directly remove the prideful identification [of self with non-self]. In <s>Brahma-mīmāṃsā</s>, however, the distinction is that [<s>viveka-jñāna</s>] has as its complement the discrimination of <s>Paramātman</s> (the Supreme Self).
In the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system, however, it has as its complement the discrimination of the <s>Ātman</s> in general — this is the general direction [of the argument].

body.translated_text: By these <s>Gītā</s> statements also, it is declared that <s>viveka-jñāna</s> (discriminative knowledge) alone is the cause of liberation. Therefore, <s>viveka-jñāna</s> alone is the direct cause of liberation through the removal of <s>avidyā</s>.

body.text:
vivekakhyātestvavidyānāśakatvameva na tu śuktirajatavivekadarśina iva punarbhramadarśanāt pratibandhakatvaṃ dṛṣṭānte paṭalakāmādidoṣabāhulyāt punarujjīvanaṃ bhramasya |
atra ca anātmanyātmābhimāne 'nādivāsanaiva doṣaḥ sarvāstikasaṃmataḥ jātamātrasyābhimāne doṣāntarānupalabdheḥ sā mithyājñānavāsanā yadā vivekakhyātiparamparājanyadṛḍhavāsanayonmūlitā tadaiva vivekasākṣātkāraniṣṭhocyate tatpūrvamavaśyaṃ vāsanāleśato mithyāṃśasya kasyāpyātmani bhānāt tasyāṃ ca vivekakhyātiniṣṭhāyāṃ jātāyāṃ na punarabhimānaḥ sambhavati vāsanākhyadoṣābhāvāditi |
yadi tu buddhipuruṣayoranyonyapratibimbanādikamavivekakāraṇaṃ doṣa iṣyate tadā tu taṃ doṣaṃ bādhitvaiva vivekasākṣātkāra udita iti na tasya punarbhramahetutvaṃ phalabalena yogajadharmāsahakṛtasyaiva tasya doṣatvakalpanāsambhavāditi |
yadyapi vivekapratiyogipadārthānāmāntyādviśeṣarūpeṇa vivekagraho na sambhavati tathāpi dṛśyatvapariṇāmitvādirūpaiḥ sāmānyavivekagrahasambhavāt prakṛtyādipadārthānāṃ viśiṣṭajñānābhāve 'pi sāmānyato vivekakhyātermokṣahetutvam |
taduktam |
body.translated_text:
The power of discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) is precisely the destruction of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), not merely an obstruction [to its recurrence] — unlike the case of one who discriminates shell from silver, where error recurs again; in the illustration [of ordinary discrimination], the error revives due to the abundance of defects such as cataracts, desire, and the like.
Here, the defect in the false identification of the self with the non-self is beginningless latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) alone — this is accepted by all realists — since no other defect is found in the case of identification occurring in one just born. When that latent impression of false knowledge is uprooted by the firm latent impression born from the succession of discriminative cognitions, only then is the culmination of the direct realization of discrimination spoken of. Prior to that, some false element necessarily appears in the self due to a residual trace of latent impression. And when that culmination of discriminative knowledge has arisen, false identification can no longer occur, because the defect called latent impression is absent.
If, however, the mutual reflection and so forth of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and <s>Puruṣa</s> is accepted as the defect that causes non-discrimination, then the direct realization of discrimination arises only after sublating that very defect — hence it cannot be a cause of renewed error, since through the force of the result, it is impossible to posit that defect as operative unless assisted by <s>yoga</s>-born <s>dharma</s>.
Although the apprehension of discrimination in the specific form of the counter-correlates of discrimination is impossible due to the ultimacy [of those entities], nevertheless, because a general discriminative apprehension through characteristics such as being perceivable, being subject to transformation, and so forth is possible, discriminative knowledge in a general form is the cause of liberation even in the absence of specific knowledge of entities such as <s>Prakṛti</s> and the rest.
As has been stated:

body.text:
ghaṭadraṣṭā ghaṭādbhinnaḥ sarvathā na ghaṭo yathā /
  dehadraṣṭā tadā dehī nāhamityādirūpataḥ // iti /
body.translated_text:
Just as the seer of a pot is entirely distinct from the pot and is in no way the pot,
so too the seer of the body, the embodied one, [realizes] 'I am not [the body]' and so forth — thus it is.

body.text:
ātmā vā are draṣṭavya ityatra tu na ātmano dṛśyatvaṃ vṛttivyāpyatve 'pi phalavyāpyatvarūpaṃ yattu bauddhairapi sukhaduḥkhādimattvenāpi buddhiranubhūyamānā svaprakāśatayā caitanyavyāpyā na bhavati yathā vedāntināmahamityanubhūyamāno 'pyātmā caitanyākhyaphalavyāpyo na bhavatītyucyate tanniḥpramāṇatvādupekṣyam |
tatpradhānādisarge utpadyate |
adharmavaśāt paśvādau dharmavaśāddevādau saṃsarati |
atattvajñānādeva dharmādharmoparañjitaṃ pralayakāle pradhāne līyate |
yadyapi pradhānapuruṣau vibhū tathāpi prakṛtireva liṅgavyavasthāṃ karoti |
liṅgaṃ sūkṣmaiḥ paramāṇubhistanmātrairupacitaṃ mānuṣādiṣu vyavatiṣṭhate naṭavat yathā naṭaḥ svarūpeṇa eko 'pi veṣāntareṇa nānārūpaḥ tathā liṅgamudarāntaḥ praviśya hastī strī pumāniti bhavati pañcaviparyayasaṃjñā bhavati yathā tamo moho mahāmohastāmiśro 'ndhatāmiśra iti |
dharmeṇa prājāpatyādyūrdhvalokaprāptiḥ |
adharmeṇa paśvādiprāptirajñānena bandhaḥ pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānenāpavargaḥ |
tacca tattvajñānaṃ guroḥ sakāśāt śāstraśravaṇenaitādṛśaṃ jāyate |
tathāhi pradhānādanyaḥ puruṣaḥ anyā buddhiḥ anyo 'haṃkāraḥ anyāni tanmātrāṇi indriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtāni ceti |
sarvaṃ kāryaṃ triguṇātmakamapi udriktaguṇāpekṣayā sāttvikādiśabdavyapadeśabhāk cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ nānāyoniṣu jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ cetayate prāpnotītyarthaḥ |
yāvat tattvajñānena liṅgaśarīraṃ na nivarttate tāvat sthūlaṃ śarīraṃ pratijanma nūtanaṃ jāyate naśyati ca |
svaprayojanābhāve 'pi pratyupakāranirapekṣaṃ sumitravat pradhānaṃ mahadādiviṣayabhūtaparyantaṃ kāryaṃ puruṣasya bhogāya mokṣāya cārabhate prakṛtiḥ puruṣasya bhedena buddhyahaṃkārādi darśayitvā nivarttate |
yathā narttakī śṛṅgārādirasairhāsyādibhāvaiśca nibaddhagītādīni raṅgasya darśayitvā nivarttate kṛtārthatvāt tadvat |
kiñca prakṛtirguṇavatī aguṇasya puṃsaḥ jagadyonibhāvena sukhaduḥkhamohātmakena śabdādiviṣayabhāvena vetyevaṃvidhairupakārairanupakāriṇaḥ puruṣasyopakurvatī paścādātmānaṃ prakāśya ahamanyā tvamanya iti nivartate sumitravat ātmanaḥ pratyupakāraṃ necchati |
body.translated_text:
'The <s>Ātman</s> indeed is to be seen' — here, however, the <s>Ātman</s> does not have the nature of being an object of perception; even though it may be pervaded by a mental modification (<s>vṛtti</s>), it has the nature of being pervaded by the result [of cognition]. As for what is said by the Buddhists — that <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), even while experienced as possessing pleasure, pain, and the like, being self-luminous, is not pervaded by consciousness — just as for the <s>Vedāntins</s>, the <s>Ātman</s>, even while experienced as 'I,' is not pervaded by the result called consciousness — that is to be disregarded since it lacks any valid proof.
From that <s>Pradhāna</s> and the rest, creation arises.
Due to <s>adharma</s> (demerit), [the soul] transmigrates into animal and other [births]; due to <s>dharma</s> (merit), into divine and other [births].
Precisely due to the absence of knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> (true principles), [the subtle body], tinged by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, dissolves into <s>Pradhāna</s> at the time of cosmic dissolution.
Although both <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> are all-pervading, it is <s>Prakṛti</s> alone that establishes the arrangement of the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>).
The subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>), constituted by the subtle atoms — the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — abides in human and other [forms] like an actor: just as an actor, though one in his own nature, assumes various forms through different costumes, so too the subtle body, entering the interior of the womb, becomes an elephant, a woman, or a man. The five kinds of error (<s>viparyaya</s>) are as follows: <s>tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmiśra</s> (gloom), and <s>andhatāmiśra</s> (blind darkness).
Through <s>dharma</s>, the attainment of the upper worlds such as that of <s>Prajāpati</s> and others.
Through <s>adharma</s>, the attainment of animal and other births; through ignorance, bondage; through the knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).
That <s>tattva</s>-knowledge of this kind arises from hearing the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) from a teacher.
Thus: <s>Puruṣa</s> is different from <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is different, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) is different, the <s>tanmātras</s>, the sense organs, and the five gross elements are each different.
All effects, though constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, receive the designation '<s>sāttvika</s>' and so forth with respect to the predominant <s>guṇa</s>. The conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> experiences — that is, attains — suffering produced by birth, old age, and death in various wombs.
As long as the subtle body (<s>liṅga-śarīra</s>) does not cease through <s>tattva</s>-knowledge, so long a new gross body is born and perishes with each birth.
Even in the absence of any purpose of its own, and without expecting any return — like a good friend — <s>Pradhāna</s> initiates the effect ranging from <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) through the sense objects to the gross elements, for the enjoyment and liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>. <s>Prakṛti</s>, having displayed <s>buddhi</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, and the rest as distinct from <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraws.
Just as a dancer, having displayed songs and the like composed with the sentiments of love (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) and so forth and the emotions of humor (<s>hāsya</s>) and others before the audience, withdraws, having fulfilled her purpose — so likewise.
Moreover, <s>Prakṛti</s>, possessing the <s>guṇas</s>, serves the <s>guṇa</s>-less <s>Puruṣa</s> — through being the source of the world, through the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, through being the form of sense objects such as sound and the like — rendering such various services to <s>Puruṣa</s> who renders no service in return; and afterward, having revealed herself — 'I am other, you are other' — she withdraws, like a good friend, not desiring any return for herself.

children.text: sargasya neśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ na svabhāvo na kālaḥ kālo 'pi yogināṃ kṣaṇarūpa eva na tu nyāyavaiśeṣikayorivātmavadakhaṇḍo nitya eko lāghavāt sa eva tattadupādyavacchinnaḥ san kṣaṇamuhūrtādivatsarāntaṃ vyavahāraṃ karotīti |
children.translated_text: The Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is not the cause of creation, nor is inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), nor is time (<s>kāla</s>) [the cause]. Time, even for the yogins, is of the nature of a moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) alone, and is not — as for the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> — undivided, eternal, and one like the <s>Ātman</s>. Due to parsimony, that very [moment], being delimited by particular limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), produces the conventional usage ranging from moment, <s>muhūrta</s>, and so forth up to a year.
But there is no separate category called 'moment' [as an independent entity].

body.text: sāṃkhyaistu dikkālāvākāśādibhya iti sūtritaṃ mahākālo vā kṣaṇādirvā pṛthak padārtho nāsti kintvākāśamevopādhibhirviśiṣṭaṃ kṣaṇādimahākālāntavyavahāraṃ kurute iti manyate |

children.text: tadetanmatadvayamapyasamañjasamityāha yogī sthireṇa kenāpyupādhinā mahākālākāśābhyāṃ kṣaṇavyavahārasyāsambhavāt |
children.translated_text: Both these views are unsatisfactory — thus the yogin says — because the conventional usage of a moment cannot arise from great time and <s>ākāśa</s> through any stable limiting adjunct.

children.text: tathāhi uttaradeśasaṃyogāvacchinnā paramāṇvādikriyā anyadvā etādṛśaṃ kiñcinmahākālākāśayoḥ kṣaṇarūpatāyāmupādhiḥ parairiṣyate tatra uktaṃ saṃyogaviśiṣṭakriyādikaṃ cet viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇatatsambandhamātraṃ tarhi trayāṇāmaparaiḥ sthiratvābhyupagamāt na taiḥ kṣaṇavyavahāraḥ sambhavati yadi ca tattebhyo 'tiriktamiṣyate na tu tanmahākāla ākāśaṃ vā tenaiva kṣaṇavyavahāropapattau tadavacchinnasyānyasya kṣaṇavyavahārahetutvakalpanāvaiyarthyāt sa ca viśiṣṭādirāsthiraḥ kṣaṇaḥ prakṛterevātibhaṅguraḥ pariṇāmaviśeṣa ityato na prakṛtipuruṣātiriktatvāpattiḥ |
children.translated_text: As follows: the action of atoms and the like delimited by conjunction with the northern direction, or some other such thing, is held by others as the limiting adjunct for the nature of a moment in great time and <s>ākāśa</s>. Regarding that: if the said conjunction-qualified action and the like [are the adjunct], and if it is merely the relation of qualifier, qualified, and their connection, then since those three are accepted by others as stable, the conventional usage of a moment cannot arise from them. If, however, something additional beyond those is accepted, and if it is neither great time nor <s>ākāśa</s>, then since the conventional usage of a moment is established by that very [additional entity] alone, positing something else delimited by it as the cause of momentary usage would be redundant. And that specific [entity] — such as a qualified [conjunction] and the like — being unstable, is a moment; it is an extremely transient particular transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s> itself. Therefore there is no need to posit anything beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tasyaiva kṣaṇasya pracayaviśeṣairmuhūrtāhorātrādirdviparārddhāntavyavahāro bhavati natvakhaṇḍo mahākālo 'sti pramāṇābhāvāt adyatyādivyavahāraḥ kṣaṇapracayenaiva kālanityatvaśrutismṛtayastu pravāhanityatāparā iti tasmādāvaśyakatvāt kṣaṇātmaka eva kālo nākhaṇḍo mahākālo 'sti nāpyākāśaṃ kālavyavahāraheturiti kiṃ tu pradhānam |
children.translated_text: Through particular accumulations of that very moment, the conventional usage of <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes), day-and-night, and so forth up to <s>dviparārdha</s> (the lifetime of <s>Brahmā</s>) arises; but there is no undivided great time, due to the absence of any valid proof. The conventional usage of 'today' and the like is accomplished by the accumulation of moments alone. The <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> passages [speaking of] the eternality of time refer to eternality in the sense of a continuous stream. Therefore, since it is necessarily of the nature of moments, time is exclusively moment-constituted; there is no undivided great time, nor is <s>ākāśa</s> the cause of temporal usage — rather, [the cause is] <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: puruṣo na badhyate na mucyate nāpi saṃsaratīti kiṃ tu nānāśrayā prakṛtireva tatheti sarvaṃ samañjasam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither bound, nor liberated, nor does he transmigrate. Rather, it is <s>Prakṛti</s> alone, abiding in various substrates, that [undergoes] all this — thus everything is consistent.

body.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, however, have taught in the <s>sūtra</s> that space (<s>dik</s>) and time (<s>kāla</s>) [arise] from <s>ākāśa</s> (space-element) and the like. [They hold that] neither great time nor the moment exists as a separate category; rather, it is <s>ākāśa</s> itself, qualified by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), that produces the conventional usage ranging from moment to great time.
Thus concludes the <s>Sāṃkhyatattvavivecana</s> (Discernment of the Sāṃkhya Principles) composed by <s>Śrī Ṣimānanda Dīkṣita</s> of <s>Kānyakubja</s>.
